The real focus should be on the business: strong AI-driven demand for NAND flash memory with 378% revenue growth, but falling flash prices pose a risk. The stock trades at a low valuation (5.6x P/E), down 70% from its 52-week high, making it potentially attractive for patient investors willing to tolerate volatility.

The article argues Alphabet is a safer investment than Anthropic stock because it profits from the relationship regardless of Anthropic's valuation, while maintaining its own profitable AI, cloud, and advertising businesses.

The complaint claims the AI model delivered disappointing training results, leading to significant launch delays, while the company made positive statements about its business prospects that lacked reasonable basis. Investors who purchased Alphabet securities between May 19, 2026 and October 28, 2026 may be eligible to recover losses, with a lead plaintiff deadline of December 1, 2026.

items.summary: In comparing two AI-focused companies, Cognizant Technology Solutions (CTSH) emerges as the better investment choice over Innodata Inc. (INOD) despite the latter's superior growth prospects. While Innodata offers higher growth potential in frontier AI and reinforcement learning with 42% revenue guidance, it faces customer concentration risks and downward earnings revisions. Cognizant presents a more balanced opportunity with diversified revenue streams, attractive valuation (10.15X P/E vs 21.37X), strong bookings of $28.7 billion, and favorable earnings revisions, making it the superior risk-adjusted investment.

items.title: Meta Platforms Just Partnered With Walmart. Here's Why Investors Should Pay Attention
items.summary: Meta has partnered with Walmart to integrate its Muse AI agent into the retailer's e-commerce platform, allowing consumers to discover products, compare prices, and complete purchases. While Meta's free cash flow has turned negative due to massive AI spending, the partnership signals potential monetization opportunities through transaction fees. Meta's core advertising business remains strong with 26% year-over-year revenue growth, positioning the company to fund its AI investments while scaling new revenue streams.

items.title: ASX's LEAP Demand Accelerates: Can Revenue Growth Stay Strong?
items.summary: ASE Technology reported record Q3 2026 revenues of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8% year-over-year, driven by surging demand for leading-edge advanced packaging (LEAP) services in AI infrastructure. The company raised its 2026 LEAP revenue projection to over $4 billion and expects it to double in 2027. ASE also increased 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $11.5 billion to meet demand exceeding available capacity.

items.title: DELL's AI Server Sales Surge: Can the Growth Momentum Continue?
items.summary: Dell Technologies reported record AI server revenues of $22 billion in Q3 fiscal 2027, representing 291% year-over-year growth and 40% of total revenues. The company secured $60.2 billion in AI server orders with a record backlog of $132.3 billion, and raised its full-year AI server revenue guidance from $74 billion to $78 billion, indicating 216% year-over-year growth. Dell's expanding customer base and strong order book position it well for sustained growth in the AI infrastructure market.

items.title: Visa (V) Up 5.9% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: Visa reported Q4 fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings of $3.48 per share, up 17% YoY and beating consensus by 1.5%, with net revenues of $12.1 billion rising 13% YoY. Strong payment volumes, cross-border activity, and transaction processing drove results, though increased operating expenses provided some offset. The company returned $5.2 billion to shareholders and raised its quarterly dividend by 16%. For FY2027, Visa projects low-double-digit revenue and operating expense growth with adjusted EPS growth in the low-teens range. The stock has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with an aggregate VGM Score of D.

items.title: Universal Health Services (UHS) Up 10.7% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: Universal Health Services stock has gained 10.7% since its last earnings report, outperforming the S&P 500. However, the company missed Q3 2026 EPS estimates despite higher patient volumes, with adjusted EPS declining 8.3% year-over-year. While revenues grew 5.3% and the company reaffirmed full-year guidance, estimate revisions have trended downward by 5.56%, leading to a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating with expectations of below-average returns ahead.

items.title: Paypal (PYPL) Up 2.2% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: PayPal reported Q3 2026 non-GAAP EPS of $1.45, beating estimates by 10.7%, driven by strong Venmo growth and expense discipline. While revenues missed expectations at $8.58B, the company raised its full-year EPS guidance to $5.60 and maintained a $6B share repurchase target. Venmo TPV grew 14% YoY to $96.81B, and financial services are expected to contribute over 20% of total monetizable volume in 2026.

items.title: Oneok (OKE) Down 8.6% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Rebound?
items.summary: ONEOK Inc. (OKE) reported Q3 2026 earnings of $2.13 per share, significantly beating the consensus estimate of $1.46, driven by higher volumes in natural gas liquids, refined products, and natural gas, plus strong optimization activities. The company raised its 2026 guidance for net income and adjusted EBITDA. However, shares have underperformed the S&P 500 by 8.6% since the earnings release. Despite upward estimate revisions, the stock carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, suggesting in-line returns ahead.

items.title: Coca-Cola (KO) Up 6.4% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: Coca-Cola reported strong Q3 2026 results, beating earnings and revenue estimates with 11% EPS growth and 7% revenue increase. The company raised its 2026 full-year guidance, projecting at least 5% organic revenue growth and 11% comparable EPS growth. Global unit case volume grew 5%, driven by strong performance in India, China, Mexico, and Brazil, with particular strength in Coca-Cola Zero Sugar (+16%). The stock has gained 6.4% in the past month and currently holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: F5 (FFIV) Down 13.3% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Rebound?
items.summary: F5 Networks reported better-than-expected Q4 fiscal 2026 results with non-GAAP EPS of $4.42 (up 0.7% YoY) and revenues of $917 million (up 13% YoY), driven by robust systems demand and AI adoption. However, shares have declined 13.3% since the earnings report. The company projects fiscal 2027 revenue growth of 8-9% with EPS of $18.00-$18.30, but faces margin pressures from higher operating expenses. F5 maintains a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Extra Space Storage (EXR) Up 11.5% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: Extra Space Storage reported Q3 2026 core FFO of $2.17 per share, beating estimates, with same-store NOI climbing 4.6%. The company raised its full-year core FFO guidance to $8.40-$8.50 and increased acquisition assumptions. Shares have gained 11.5% since the earnings report, outperforming the S&P 500. However, the stock carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with an aggregate VGM Score of F, suggesting in-line returns ahead.

items.title: AI in Healthcare Market to Reach US$ 1,078.42 Billion by 2034 at 45.3% CAGR, as Generative AI Transforms Healthcare Delivery | Exclusive Report by The Insight Partners
items.summary: The global AI in healthcare market is projected to grow from US$ 39.55 billion in 2025 to US$ 1,078.42 billion by 2034, with a 45.3% CAGR. Generative AI, enterprise adoption, and cloud deployment are driving growth, with Asia Pacific expected to register a 47.5% CAGR. North America leads with 41.2% market share, while large enterprises account for 69.6% of revenue.

items.title: MCD's Entry-Level Value Push: A Key Catalyst for Its 2027 Outlook?
items.summary: McDonald's is testing affordable menu bundles at 1,900 restaurants with franchisees adopting similar offerings at 4,000 more locations, covering over 40% of the U.S. system. The initiative aims to attract budget-conscious consumers and improve traffic after comparable sales declined 0.2% in Q3. Extra Value Meals showed 7% year-over-year unit sales growth. A nationwide rollout is expected in early 2027, with earnings estimates implying 5.9% and 5.2% growth for 2026 and 2027 respectively.

items.summary: GE HealthCare Technologies announced that its Omni 128 cm total body PET/CT system has entered FDA 510(k) review following CE Mark approval in November 2025. The system enables up to 88% reduction in PET dose or 86% reduction in scan time, imaging from head to thigh in a single position. The company also submitted its Omni 64 cm configuration for FDA review, offering up to 73% shorter scan times. The global PET scanners market is projected to reach $2.96 billion by 2026 with a 5% CAGR through 2034.

items.title: VRTX Down as FDA Extends Review Timeline for Povetacicept BLA
items.summary: Vertex Pharmaceuticals' stock dropped 7.3% after the FDA extended the review timeline for povetacicept's biologics license application by three months, with a final decision now expected on February 28, 2027. The FDA classified additional information submitted by Vertex as a major amendment requiring more review time. Meanwhile, competitor Vera Therapeutics surged 16.7% as investors viewed the delay as an opportunity for its marketed IgAN drug Trutakna to strengthen its market position.

items.title: Netflix Stock and Higher Content Spend: Can Margins Hold Firm in 2027?
items.summary: Netflix faces a critical margin test in 2027 as elevated content spending and live programming investments increase. While Q3 2026 showed strong 34.6% operating margins, Q4 guidance projects a decline to 26%. The company plans ad-tier expansion into 15 new countries in 2027 to support revenue, but 2027 margins will depend on whether higher content spend drives stronger engagement. Netflix shares have underperformed year-to-date, trading at a premium valuation with a Hold rating.

items.title: Alphabet Drops 15% in a Year: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: Alphabet shares have underperformed, dropping 14.7% over the past year due to aggressive AI infrastructure spending, deteriorating free cash flow, and slowing Search revenue growth. While the company faces near-term headwinds from $51.4B Q3 capital expenditure and declining 2027 earnings estimates, long-term prospects remain encouraging driven by robust Google Cloud demand (103% revenue surge), expanding TPU system sales, and accelerating Gemini adoption. The stock is rated a Hold with a premium valuation relative to the sector.

items.title: Copart Gears Up to Report Q1 Earnings: Here's What to Expect
items.summary: Copart is set to report Q1'27 results on December 1 with consensus estimates of 40 cents per share and $1.18B in revenue. While international business shows strong growth and the ACV Auctions acquisition diversifies revenue, elevated operating expenses and margin pressures pose concerns. The company carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) with a negative Earnings ESP of -5.60%, suggesting limited likelihood of an earnings beat.

The company forecasts ~75% revenue growth for fiscal 2028. However, competitors AMD and Broadcom are gaining ground with their own AI accelerators and networking solutions. NVIDIA trades at a forward P/E of 9.90, below sector average, and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

The company reported a 7% sequential increase in one-year backlog in Q3 2026 and expects 10% sequential product revenue growth in Q4 2026. Equipment installation at Fab-2 is planned for Q2 2027, with potential capacity reaching nearly 5x that of Fab-1. Competitors Monolithic Power Systems and Texas Instruments are also aggressively expanding capacity to capture AI data center power management opportunities.

items.title: Diodes Rides on AI, Automotive & Industrial Traction: Should You Buy?

Q3 results showed computing revenues up 33%, automotive up 60%, and industrial up 50% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS surging 219%. The company expects 40.4% revenue growth in Q4 2026 and ~30% growth for the full year, significantly exceeding its historical 10% CAGR. Zacks rates DIOD as a Strong Buy.

items.title: GFS' AI Optical Connectivity Business Gains Traction: Can it Sustain?
items.summary: GlobalFoundries (GFS) is experiencing strong growth in its communications infrastructure and data center business, driven by AI data center demand for optical connectivity. Q3 2026 revenues in this segment surged 81% year-over-year to $316M, with management raising full-year growth guidance to 60-70%. The company targets $1 billion in annualized silicon photonics revenue by end of 2027 and plans to nearly triple capacity. However, sustained demand, timely capacity expansion, and successful customer production ramps remain critical to achieving growth targets.

items.title: Could CMS' Proposed Star Ratings Changes Slow ELV's MA Recovery?
items.summary: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services has proposed significant changes to its Star Ratings system that could reduce quality bonus payments for Medicare Advantage insurers. Peers Humana and UnitedHealth Group could also face pressure, with UnitedHealth facing a steeper potential decline from 68% to 9%.

items.title: If an AI Bubble Bursts, This Is the Only Tech Stock I Want to Own
items.summary: The article argues that Apple is the most resilient tech stock if an AI bubble bursts. Unlike competitors pouring billions into AI infrastructure, Apple rents AI capabilities and runs most AI on-device efficiently. With 2.5 billion active devices, 1.5 billion paid subscriptions, and strong services revenue, Apple has a defensible business model independent of AI spending. However, the current AI boom is hurting Apple through elevated memory chip costs, forcing price increases on devices.

items.title: Why Hewlett Packard Enterprise Stock Fell 16% Today
items.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) stock plummeted 16% despite beating Q4 earnings estimates and raising fiscal 2027 guidance. While AI server demand is strong with orders up 88% and a 90% year-over-year backlog increase, investors were disappointed by shrinking profit margins. Operating margins are expected to decline to 14-15% in fiscal 2027 from 15.1% in fiscal 2026, as AI servers—though high-volume—carry lower profitability. Component supply constraints for memory and NAND are expected to persist through at least mid-2028, limiting the company's ability to capitalize on surging demand.

items.summary: Intel stock dropped 2.3% after Nvidia disclosed it sold 25% of its Intel stake (reducing from 214.8M to 161.1M shares) while simultaneously increasing its SpaceX position by 6%. items.title: Where Will Nvidia Stock Be in 3 Years?
items.summary: Nvidia faces significant uncertainty following CEO Jensen Huang's resignation amid allegations of affairs and potential national security concerns related to chip exports to China. The article examines two competing narratives: bulls point to Nvidia's dominant AI market position and cheap valuation (21x trailing earnings), while bears question whether Huang artificially inflated demand through strategic investments in AI startups and whether $200 billion in idle GPUs indicate demand was overstated. The key factor determining Nvidia's stock performance over three years will be its ability to maintain profit margins amid competition from custom chips and AMD.

The lead plaintiff deadline is January 12, 2027, for investors who purchased Intel securities between July 23, 2026 and October 29, 2026.

items.title: 3 Stocks in a Bull Rally Right Now

items.title: Not Nvidia. Not Broadcom. This Is the AI Chip Stock I’d Buy Before the Year Ends.
items.summary: While Nvidia and Broadcom are major AI beneficiaries, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) is positioned as the superior investment choice. TSMC holds a 73% market share in chip foundry manufacturing and has a virtual monopoly on advanced AI chip production, giving it pricing power regardless of which company wins the AI race. With 66.4% gross margins, 58.7% operating margins, and expected Q4 revenue growth of 55-61%, TSMC's recent 7% pullback presents a buying opportunity before year-end.

items.title: Marvell and Intel Are Both Down at Least 50% From Their 2026 Highs. Only 1 Is a Stock I’d Buy.
items.summary: Both Marvell Technology and Intel have fallen over 50% from their 2026 highs amid AI spending concerns. Intel's stock collapsed due to disappointing PC and foundry business results, weak guidance, and massive capex spending plans. Marvell, despite a 50% decline from highs, remains the better buy as it shows strong AI chip demand with 37% revenue growth, high profitability (59% gross margin), and minimal capex spending, with projections for 567% revenue growth by 2031.

items.title: TTMI's AI Capacity Expansion Accelerates: Will Revenue Growth Follow?
items.summary: TTM Technologies (TTMI) is accelerating its manufacturing capacity expansion with over $1.3 billion invested through 2029 to capture growing demand for advanced PCBs used in AI data centers. Data Center and Networking sales surged 115% year-over-year in Q3 2026, reaching 41% of revenues, with N+M boards expected to hit 50% by 2027. items.title: 3 Stocks to Buy as Nvidia's Empire Potentially Crumbles
items.summary: Following CEO Jensen Huang's resignation amid personal scandals and Anthropic's breakthrough in porting AI models to AMD GPUs in just three days, Nvidia's dominance in AI infrastructure is being challenged. items.title: Home Depot Q3 Earnings Meet Estimates, Sales Beat on Comps Growth

Comparable sales rose 2.2% driven by higher average ticket ($93.09), though customer transactions declined slightly. However, gross margin contracted 60 basis points to 32.8% due to cost of sales outpacing revenue growth. Operating margin also narrowed 30 basis points. Management updated FY26 guidance projecting 4.5% sales growth and 1.4% comparable sales growth.

items.title: Astera Labs vs. Amphenol: Which Connectivity Stock Is the Better Buy?
items.summary: Amphenol (APH) emerges as the stronger connectivity stock compared to Astera Labs (ALAB), backed by diversified revenues and broader market exposure. APH's IT datacom business surged 117% YoY with strong optical connectivity capabilities from the CommScope acquisition. Both stocks carry a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

However, online marketing revenues fell 22% YoY, and operating margins contracted to 6% due to higher AI cloud costs. The company continues expanding its autonomous ride-hailing service Apollo Go to 30 cities globally.

items.title: Home Depot's Best Comp of the Year Arrives With a Thinner Margin
items.summary: Home Depot exceeded Q3 revenue expectations with $43.4B in sales (up 4.9%) and 2.2% comparable sales growth, but margins contracted significantly. Gross margin fell to 32.8% from 33.4% year-over-year, with the company guiding sales to the high end while margins move to the low end of guidance. The margin pressure stems from acquisition-driven growth through lower-margin professional distribution channels. Management also implied fourth-quarter comparable sales will decelerate to around 1% despite strong current momentum.

items.title: Zscaler vs. Okta: Which Cloud Cybersecurity Stock Has the Edge?
items.summary: Okta and Zscaler are competing in the cloud cybersecurity market with different approaches. items.title: INCY Wins European Commission Nod For Skin Disease Drug
items.summary: Incyte announced European Commission approval for Povofortay (povorcitinib) 45 mg and 75 mg for treating moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa in adults. The approval is based on STOP-HS1 and STOP-HS2 studies showing durable efficacy through Week 54, with up to 71.4% of patients achieving HiSCR50. Povofortay is the first once-daily oral treatment approved in the EU for this indication. FDA review for U.S. approval is ongoing, with anticipated approval in Q1 2027.

items.title: PBR Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Output Growth and Pricing Scrutiny

items.title: Eaton vs. Vertiv: Which Industrials Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

items.title: ISRG EPS Climbs 25% to $3: Is Innovation Driving Profitable Growth?

Nvidia and other AI stocks rallied on the news, but the sector's biggest risk is now the cost of financing data center buildouts rather than demand itself.

items.title: Bull of the Day: Ingram Micro (INGM)
items.summary: Ingram Micro (INGM) reported record fiscal Q3 2026 results with net sales jumping 20.8% to $15.2 billion, driven by strong GPU and AI infrastructure demand. The company beat earnings estimates for the eighth consecutive quarter and raised full-year guidance. With a forward P/E of 7.9 and P/S ratio of 0.1, the stock is trading at deep value levels while benefiting from the AI revolution.

items.title: Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights Kinder Morgan, The Williams and MPLX LP
items.summary: The Oil & Gas - Production and Pipelines industry faces gloomy prospects with a Zacks Industry Rank of #153, driven by conservative upstream spending, high debt loads, and the shift toward renewables. However, Kinder Morgan, The Williams Companies, and MPLX LP are well-positioned to navigate uncertainties through stable fee-based revenues and exposure to growing LNG demand and data center power needs.

items.title: Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights Take-Two Interactive Software, Rush Street Interactive and Accel Entertainment
items.summary: The gaming industry faces headwinds from macroeconomic pressures, regulatory complexities, and weakness in Macau's gaming revenues. However, digital gaming and sports betting present growth opportunities. Three gaming stocks highlighted are Take-Two Interactive Software (strong pipeline and digital revenue), Rush Street Interactive (online casino and sports betting expansion), and Accel Entertainment (distributed gaming operations expansion).

items.summary: Nvidia faces significant uncertainty following CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation amid scandal, just before reporting earnings. The departure threatens Nvidia's flat management structure and raises concerns about the company's leadership succession. Additionally, Huang's role as a key financier of the AI ecosystem creates broader implications for AI infrastructure companies. The market has entered a new regime with rising volatility, Fed rate hikes, and a shift toward defensive sectors, suggesting the easy gains from the AI boom may be ending.

items.title: Prediction: Nov. 18 Will Be a Huge Day for AI Power Stocks. Here’s Why.
items.summary: Nvidia's fiscal Q3 earnings report on Nov. 17 could significantly impact AI power stocks on Nov. 18. The report will show whether AI infrastructure spending is accelerating or moderating. Strong results and positive guidance could boost energy companies supplying power to data centers, including Constellation Energy, Bloom Energy, and Energy Transfer, which have benefited from increased AI infrastructure investments.

items.title: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Overhauled Berkshire's Portfolio for a 3rd Straight Quarter, Reducing 6 Stocks and Piling Into a Hot Tech IPO
items.summary: Greg Abel, who took over as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway after Warren Buffett's retirement, continues to reshape the company's $364 billion portfolio in Q3 2026. Abel reduced stakes in six stocks including Bank of America (9th consecutive quarter of selling) and VeriSign, while significantly increasing investments in AI and tech stocks, notably acquiring a 4% stake in Bending Spoons through a $330 million private placement. This marks a notable shift from Buffett's traditional investment approach toward growth-oriented technology companies.

items.title: NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA): Treasury Secretary Reportedly Questions Company’s Revenues, Stock Sinks Again -- HBSS
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent questioned whether NVIDIA's earnings were inflated by inappropriate sales to China. The scrutiny follows reports that NVIDIA stopped reporting Singapore sales and involves an investigation into a partner company allegedly helping circumvent U.S. export restrictions. CEO Jensen Huang departed amid revelations of a personal relationship with a Megaspeed executive suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. A securities class action lawsuit alleges NVIDIA misled investors about these ties and export compliance.

items.title: If I Could Buy and Hold Only 1 AI Hyperscaler Through 2030, It Would Be This One
items.summary: The article argues that Amazon is the best single AI hyperscaler to buy and hold through 2030. Despite concerns about heavy spending on data center infrastructure, Amazon's dual revenue engines (e-commerce and AWS), strong track record of wise capital allocation, and upcoming external sales of custom AI chips position it well for long-term growth. AWS generates 60% of operating income and is expanding its AI offerings, while Amazon's custom chip business reached a $25 billion annual revenue run rate.

items.title: DUOLINGO STOCKHOLDER ALERT: Bragar Eagel & Squire, P.C. Urges Duolingo, Inc. Investors with Large Losses to Contact the Firm Regarding Their Rights Before December 7th
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Duolingo in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania on behalf of investors who purchased shares between May 2, 2025 and February 26, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that Duolingo made false or misleading statements regarding Daily Active User growth rates, failed to disclose that increased ad volume and subscription upsells were causing user friction and negatively impacting DAU growth, and concealed that rapidly generated AI content was degrading product quality and user experience. Investors have until December 7, 2026 to apply to be appointed as lead plaintiff.

items.title: ALPHABET (GOOG) ALERT: Bragar Eagel & Squire, P.C Urgently Reminds Alphabet Inc. Investors to Contact the Firm Seeking Lead Plaintiff Role Before December 1st
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Alphabet Inc. for allegedly making materially false statements about its business during May-July 2026. The complaint alleges that Alphabet failed to disclose that the Gemini 3.5 Pro was delivering disappointing training results and would face significant launch delays. Investors who purchased Alphabet securities during this period have until December 1, 2026 to apply as lead plaintiff.

items.title: XP Inc.A (XP) Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates
items.summary: XP Inc.A reported quarterly earnings of $0.52 per share, missing the consensus estimate of $0.53, though it surpassed revenue expectations at $1 billion. The stock has underperformed the S&P 500 by 15.9% year-to-date and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating. The company's industry, Financial - Miscellaneous Services, ranks in the bottom 42% of Zacks industries.

items.title: C3.ai, Inc. (AI) Sees a More Significant Dip Than Broader Market: Some Facts to Know
items.summary: C3.ai stock declined 9.64% in recent trading, significantly outpacing broader market losses. The company faces headwinds with projected revenue declining 29.36% quarter-over-quarter and 10.89% year-over-year, though earnings are expected to improve. The stock currently holds a Zacks Rank of #4 (Sell).

items.title: NVIDIA After Jensen: What's Next for the AI Trade?
items.summary: NVIDIA's stock has declined over 35% from its 52-week high following Jensen Huang's exit as CEO, with CFO Colette Kress appointed as interim leader. The article discusses whether this represents a buying opportunity or a wait-and-see situation, while examining how competitors like AMD and Broadcom may capitalize on NVIDIA's troubles. The departure also raises questions about NVIDIA's financing arrangements for neocloud providers and the broader implications for the AI sector.

items.title: Top Stock Picks for Week of November 16, 2026
items.summary: Zacks has identified Hinge Health (HNGE) and Western Digital (WDC) as Strong Buy stocks with significant growth potential. Hinge Health, a digital musculoskeletal care platform, is projected to double revenue between 2025-2027 with expanding AI capabilities and corporate client growth. Western Digital reported better-than-expected results driven by cloud and AI data storage demand, with improved margins and strong cash generation.

items.title: Sandisk’s Stock Split Is Coming on Nov. 19. Should You Buy Before It Happens?
items.summary: Sandisk is executing an 8-for-1 stock split on Nov. 19, 2026, which could attract retail and options traders by lowering the share price from ~$819 to ~$102. However, the more compelling investment thesis is the company's strong growth in AI data center storage, with data center revenue jumping 61% sequentially to $4.8 billion and overall revenue up 378% year-over-year. While memory markets are cyclical and current favorable conditions may not persist, the author recommends buying both before and after the split due to the company's expanding AI infrastructure opportunity.

items.title: AI Spending Accelerates: 3 Hyperscaler Stocks for Strong 2027 Returns
items.summary: Despite recent AI stock sell-offs and valuation concerns, hyperscalers continue massive infrastructure investments with strong cloud demand and enterprise AI adoption. Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft are positioned as high-conviction opportunities for 2027, supported by accelerating backlogs, revenue growth, and improving monetization of AI investments. Global AI spending is projected to reach $4.05 trillion in 2027, up 47.5% year-over-year.

items.title: Target vs. Walmart Stock:  Which is the Better Buy Ahead of Q3 Earnings?
items.summary: Target and Walmart are reporting Q3 earnings this week amid consumer spending concerns ahead of the holiday season. Target has significantly outperformed Walmart in 2026 (70% vs 16% YTD return) and trades at a more attractive valuation (17X forward earnings vs Walmart's 40X), while offering a higher dividend yield of 3% versus 0.8%. However, Walmart demonstrates stronger long-term performance and a more defensive business model. Target receives a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) while Walmart gets a #3 (Hold), though investors should await Q3 results and holiday guidance before making decisions.

items.title: ACC Granted Leave to Intervene Before EU General Court in Broadcom Legal Privilege Case
items.summary: The Association of Corporate Counsel (ACC) has been granted permission by the General Court of the European Union to intervene in the Broadcom and VMware International v Commission case (T-280/26). The case addresses how legal professional privilege applies to legal advice from outside the EU, a critical issue for in-house counsel operating globally. ACC's intervention will provide the court with insights into how in-house legal departments function across jurisdictions and the importance of confidential legal advice for compliance and governance.

items.title: Why Intel Stock Is Falling Monday
items.summary: Intel stock fell 6.7% on Monday as chip stocks broadly sold off ahead of Nvidia's earnings report. The decline was driven by market uncertainty following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure due to personal misconduct involving a Chinese intelligence asset. Additionally, Intel faces a new lawsuit alleging delayed disclosure of weak PC sales and excess inventory ahead of its October plunge. The author attributes the decline primarily to general market jitters rather than the lawsuit.

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway's Railroad Earned 19% More Last Quarter. Its Insurance Underwriting Earned 43% Less.
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway's Q3 2026 earnings showed mixed results: insurance underwriting fell 43% while railroad freight operations (BNSF) rose 19.3%. The article highlights how Berkshire's diversified portfolio across multiple quality businesses allows it to weather underperformance in any single segment, demonstrating the strength of its multi-sector investment strategy under new CEO Greg Abel.

items.title: SHAREHOLDER ALERT: Bronstein Gewirtz & Grossman, LLC Announces Class Action Against Lennar Corporation (NYSE: LEN) — Investors Who Suffered Losses Are Encouraged to Contact the Firm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Lennar Corporation (NYSE: LEN) alleging that the company made false and misleading statements regarding its financial performance. The complaint claims Lennar improperly capitalized costs related to land bank option agreements and that its Millrose subsidiary purchased completed homes at above-market prices while renting them at losses, contrary to its stated purpose. These transactions allegedly artificially bolstered reported sales and financial results while concealing weakening home demand. Investors who purchased Lennar securities between February 7, 2025 and October 2, 2026 may be eligible to recover losses, with a lead plaintiff deadline of January 11, 2027.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges AppLovin Corporation Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against AppLovin Corporation alleging securities fraud. The complaint claims that between February 12, 2026 and August 5, 2026, the company made false or misleading statements regarding its generative AI video creative feature, overstating AI model improvements and the benefits of its 'virtuous cycle' value proposition. Investors who purchased AppLovin securities during this period are encouraged to join the case.

items.title: PayPal Stock Trades at a Discount: Bargain Buy or Value Trap?
items.summary: PayPal trades at a significant valuation discount (10.11x forward P/E) compared to Visa and Mastercard, reflecting investor skepticism about its turnaround prospects. While the company shows encouraging signs through Venmo growth (14% volume increase), Braintree momentum (10% growth), and strong cash generation ($2B adjusted free cash flow), weak branded-checkout growth (1-2%) remains a concern. Management raised 2026 EPS guidance to $5.60 and targets $6.5B in adjusted free cash flow, but sustained recovery depends on reviving checkout growth and transaction margins.

items.title: Sandisk Is Splitting Its Stock 8-for-1. Here’s the Number I’d Check Before Buying.
items.summary: Sandisk announced an 8-for-1 stock split effective Nov. 20, 2026. While stock splits generate investor excitement, the article argues that investors should focus on the company's gross margins rather than the new share price. Sandisk's gross margins have surged from ~10% in 2024 to ~85%, but the key question is whether these margins can be sustained. Since margins are driven by memory pricing and supply-demand dynamics, any slowdown in AI infrastructure investment could cause margins to collapse. The stock trades at a P/S ratio of 4.6, significantly above its 2025 average of 1.7, meaning the market has already priced in major profitability improvements.

items.title: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent Just Issued a Blistering Warning to Nvidia
items.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent expressed serious concerns about Nvidia following former CEO Jensen Huang's resignation over allegations of an extramarital affair with a woman linked to illegal chip diversions to China. Bessent called for a 'dramatic shakeup' at Nvidia, demanded answers within 10 days, and opposed Huang's potential return as CEO, citing national security concerns and potential compliance violations. The warning highlights divisions within the Trump administration, as Commerce Secretary Lutnick and President Trump have been more supportive of Huang.

items.title: Is GEV Boosting Its Position in the Global Power Infrastructure Market?
items.summary: GE Vernova (GEV) is strengthening its position in the global power infrastructure market, signing 11 GW of new gas equipment contracts and converting 13 GW of reservations into orders in Q3 2026. The company's Electrification business saw revenues surge 51% to $3.9 billion with a 60% increase in equipment backlog. GEV expects total backlog to exceed $200 billion by Q4 2026 and raised full-year guidance. However, the stock trades at a premium valuation (30.25X forward P/E vs. 20.15X industry average) and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: ADM Raises 2026 Earnings Outlook as Biofuel Strength Lifts Profit
items.summary: Archer-Daniels-Midland (ADM) raised its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $5.50-$5.80 from $5.15-$5.60, driven by stronger year-to-date execution and favorable North American biofuel economics. Carbohydrate Solutions profit surged 40% to $470M, while crushing profit gained $298M. The company expects broad fourth-quarter profit growth across all segments, though trade, policy, and commodity risks remain headwinds.

items.title: ARM's 50% Licensing Revenue Surge Signals Strong AI-Driven Demand
items.summary: ARM Holdings reported robust Q2 fiscal 2027 results with licensing revenues jumping 50% to $773M and total revenues rising 27% to $1.44B, driven by growing AI infrastructure demand and major licensing deals. Royalty revenues increased 8% to $670M, supported by wider adoption of Armv9 architecture. However, the company faces near-term volatility from licensing agreement timing and smartphone market pressures.

items.title: NVO's Hemophilia A Treatment Gets EC Nod, Data Presented on CagriSema
items.summary: Novo Nordisk received European Commission approval for Frehemgo (denecimig), a next-generation bispecific antibody for hemophilia A prophylaxis. The company also presented positive Phase III data for CagriSema, showing 20.7-21.0% weight loss at 68 weeks versus 2.0% for placebo, with FDA decision expected in Q4 2026. However, Novo faces intensifying competition from Eli Lilly's obesity and diabetes drugs.

items.title: RIG Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates as Rig Utilization Falls
items.summary: Transocean (RIG) reported breakeven Q3 adjusted EPS, missing estimates as contract drilling revenues declined 8.9% year-over-year to $937 million. Fleet utilization fell to 74.7% with ultra-deepwater revenues down 15.2%. However, the company added $2 billion in new contracts and is advancing its $200 million synergy-targeted acquisition of Valaris, with shareholder approval scheduled for November 24, 2026.

items.title: Diamondback Eyes $5B Double Eagle Deal to Deepen Permian Dominance
items.summary: Diamondback Energy (FANG) is nearing a roughly $5 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of Double Eagle V, an EnCap Investments-backed oil and gas producer in the Midland Basin. This follows FANG's $4.1 billion acquisition of Double Eagle IV in February 2025 and its $26 billion merger with Endeavor Energy Resources in 2024, reflecting the company's strategy of consolidating high-quality assets within the Permian Basin rather than pursuing geographic diversification.

items.title: EMCOR's P1 Acquisition: Is This a New Growth Driver for 2027?
items.summary: EMCOR Group announced an agreement to acquire P1 Construction in an all-cash transaction expected to close in Q1 2027. P1, generating $600-650 million in 2026 revenues, specializes in mechanical and electrical contracting for mission-critical infrastructure including data centers. The acquisition strengthens EMCOR's competitive position amid strong demand, supported by a record $18.57 billion backlog with $8.74 billion from data centers.

items.title: Netflix Stock Now Trades at a 70% Discount to Its Peak Valuation, and One Number Is to Blame
items.summary: Netflix shares have fallen 32% year-to-date and now trade at a 70% discount to their June 2025 peak, driven primarily by decelerating revenue growth. Management forecasts Q4 2026 revenue growth of just 11.5%, down from 17.6% in Q4 2025, while advertising revenue guidance was cut to $2.7 billion from an original $3 billion projection. The streaming giant faces intensifying competition from YouTube, short-form video platforms, and other streaming services, making it difficult to add subscribers and maintain pricing power in an increasingly mature market.

items.title: Nvidia, AI, and the Tech Sector's Earnings Outlook
items.summary: Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia's leadership represents a significant setback for the chipmaker, though its status as an AI sector bellwether should help retain talent. The news comes as Nvidia prepares Q3 earnings. Meanwhile, the broader AI trade faces scrutiny over capital expenditure sustainability, with independent data center operators like CoreWeave facing funding constraints unlike major hyperscalers. Q3 earnings show broad strength with 454 S&P 500 companies reporting +24.9% YoY earnings growth and 82.4% beating EPS expectations.

items.title: AER or WAB: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
items.summary: AerCap (AER) is identified as the superior value opportunity compared to Westinghouse Air Brake Technologies (WAB) in the Transportation - Equipment and Leasing sector. AER holds a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) with a forward P/E of 7.88 and PEG ratio of 0.59, while WAB has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) with a forward P/E of 27.16 and PEG ratio of 1.67. AER received a Value grade of B versus WAB's F grade, indicating AER presents better valuation metrics and earnings outlook.

items.title: PLTR Raises 2026 Guidance as Q3 AI Demand Drives 96% Revenue Growth
items.summary: Palantir Technologies raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $8.530-$8.534 billion following a Q3 earnings beat with 96% year-over-year revenue growth. U.S. commercial revenues surged 148% to $984 million, exceeding government revenues for the first time. The company maintains a 62% adjusted operating margin while increasing investments in AI platform development and technical hiring.

items.title: Costco Hits 52-Week High on Strong Sales and Special Dividend
items.summary: Costco reached a 52-week high of $1,109.50 with shares up 28.3% year-to-date, driven by strong October sales growth of 12.6% and digital sales surge of 22.5%. The company announced a $30 special dividend and $4B buyback program. However, its forward P/E ratio of 47.75 significantly exceeds the industry average of 30.19, suggesting much of the optimism may already be priced in and limiting near-term upside potential.

items.title: 5 Dividend Growth Stocks to Buy as NVDA CEO Resignation Rattles Market
items.summary: Following NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's resignation that rattled tech stocks, investors are turning to dividend growth stocks for stability. Five stocks—J.M. Smucker, Taiwan Semiconductor, Corning, Lockheed Martin, and Cardinal Health—are highlighted as solid choices offering consistent dividend growth, reliable cash flow, and downside protection amid market volatility and regulatory uncertainty.

items.title: Is PLTR Stock a Buy or a Hold as Growth Battles a Premium Valuation?
items.summary: Palantir Technologies (PLTR) demonstrates exceptional 96% revenue growth and strong cash generation, but trades at a premium valuation of 70.2X forward earnings compared to its sub-industry average of 26.9X. While the company's AI-driven expansion and $10.4 billion in liquidity are positive, cloud commitments and customer concentration risks warrant caution. The stock receives a Hold rating with balanced risk-reward dynamics.

items.title: 1 No-Brainer AI Infrastructure Stock to Buy Hand Over Fist in November
items.summary: Alphabet is highlighted as a compelling AI infrastructure investment opportunity in November. The company's Google Cloud division saw revenue jump over 100% in the recent quarter, with a backlog exceeding $560 billion. Despite investor concerns about hyperscaler capital spending, Alphabet's strong financials, visibility through its backlog, and dominant search market position (90% share) make it attractive at 22x forward earnings.

items.title: SCHW Client Assets Hit $13.27T in October: Will the Momentum Continue?
items.summary: Charles Schwab reported strong October 2026 results with client assets reaching $13.27 trillion (up 12% YoY) and record core net new assets of $66.5 billion. The company opened 409,000 new brokerage accounts and saw daily average trades jump 23% to 10.6 million. However, rising expenses and AI-enabled fintech competition pose challenges ahead. Management expects 2026 net interest margin toward the lower end of its 3.00%-3.10% guidance range.

items.title: Tyson Foods' Q4 Earnings Miss Estimates as Beef Losses Widen
items.summary: Tyson Foods (TSN) reported Q4 fiscal 2026 earnings that missed expectations with adjusted EPS of 61 cents versus consensus of 65 cents, down 47% year-over-year. While sales exceeded estimates at $14.6 billion, the company faced significant headwinds in its Beef segment with operating losses widening to $171 million due to higher cattle costs and tight supplies. For fiscal 2027, TSN projects sales to decline 3.5-5.5% and adjusted operating income of $1.7-$2.15 billion, with the Beef segment expected to post losses of $300 million to $100 million profit.

items.title: Add These 4 Top-Performing Liquid Stocks to Maximize Returns
items.summary: A stock screening analysis identified four companies meeting strict criteria for liquidity and asset efficiency: e.l.f. Beauty (ELF), Hinge Health (HNGE), MACOM Technology Solutions (MTSI), and Semtech Corporation (SMTC). These stocks were selected from over 7,700 candidates based on liquidity ratios, above-average asset utilization, Zacks Rank #1 ratings, and strong growth scores. All four companies demonstrated impressive recent financial performance with significant revenue growth and positive guidance.

items.title: Can Applied Materials Capitalize on Rising HBM Demand in 2026?
items.summary: Applied Materials (AMAT) is capitalizing on surging AI infrastructure demand, with DRAM revenues jumping 52% year-over-year to record levels in fiscal Q3 2026. The company raised its advanced packaging revenue growth outlook to over 70% from 50%, driven by high-bandwidth memory (HBM) demand. However, AMAT stock trades at a premium valuation (P/S of 6.38X vs. industry 3.01X) and carries a Hold rating, with growth dependent on sustained customer capital spending in the cyclical memory industry.

items.title: Is Sandisk (SNDK) Stock a Buy After Its 8-for-1 Split?
items.summary: Sandisk announced an 8-for-1 stock split effective November 19, 2026. The article explains that stock splits are largely cosmetic accounting events that don't fundamentally change a company's value. While the number of shares increases eightfold and the price decreases proportionally, the underlying business remains unchanged. The author notes Sandisk's strength in digital data storage and memory chips for AI data centers, adding it to their watch list as a promising opportunity.

items.title: Is TSM Still a Buy as AI Growth Faces Heavy Spending and Valuation?
items.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM) reported strong Q3 2026 results with 41.2% revenue growth and 57.5% earnings growth, driven by AI demand and advanced-node adoption. The company raised its 2026 revenue growth outlook to 44% and maintained capital spending of $60-64 billion. However, elevated valuation ratios, margin pressure from overseas fabs and N2 ramp costs, and substantial capital intensity warrant selective buying rather than aggressive entry.

items.title: Larry Ellison Has Lost $145 Billion in Net Worth Over the Past Year as Oracle Stock Fell 59% From Its Peak. Here's Why Oracle's Heavy Concentration in OpenAI Has Wall Street Nervous.
items.summary: Oracle's stock has plummeted 44-50% over the past year, causing founder Larry Ellison to lose approximately $145 billion in net worth. Wall Street is concerned about Oracle's heavy reliance on OpenAI as a customer, with an estimated $300 billion (nearly half) of Oracle's $664 billion backlog coming from OpenAI. While Oracle's cloud segment shows strong 62% growth and the company trades at a reasonable 15x forward earnings, the concentration risk is significant given Oracle's massive $90-95 billion annual capital expenditure commitments funded through debt, creating vulnerability if OpenAI scales back orders.

items.title: Bank of America Moves to Settle Fake-Accounts Lawsuit: What's Next?
items.summary: Bank of America has reached a settlement in principle in a class-action lawsuit over unauthorized customer accounts opened by employees to meet sales targets. The settlement, pending court approval by January 11, 2027, could reduce legal costs and reputational risks, though the financial impact remains uncertain. BAC's shares have underperformed the industry in the past six months, and earnings estimates have been revised lower.

items.title: GE Aerospace Faces Cost Inflation: A Threat to Margin Growth?
items.summary: GE Aerospace is investing over $1 billion to expand its global maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) network and manufacturing capabilities, capitalizing on rising demand for engines and aftermarket services. However, the company faces margin pressure as cost of sales increased 17.2% year-over-year and operating profit margin contracted 80 basis points to 19.9% in Q3 2026, driven by higher production costs, unfavorable product mix, and persistent inflation.

items.title: CBRS Q3 Earnings Call Spotlights Capacity Delays and 2027 Growth
items.summary: Cerebras Systems (CBRS) exceeded Q3 expectations with $230.87M revenue and 13-cent EPS, raising its 2026 outlook to $940-960M. The company secured new hyperscaler agreements with Microsoft, AWS, and Oracle, but acknowledged delays in OpenAI capacity deliveries due to data center infrastructure constraints. Management expects to return to schedule in H2 2027 and projects tripling revenue in 2027 through capacity expansion and margin improvements.

items.title: DOW's Shares Surge 41% YTD: What's Driving the Momentum?

(DUOL) shareholders who purchased shares between May 2, 2025 and February 26, 2026 to seek legal counsel before the December 7, 2026 deadline for a securities class action lawsuit. The complaint also claims the company used low-quality AI-generated content that damaged user experience and financial performance.

items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is reminding investors who purchased securities of The Ensign Group, Inc. between February 10, 2022 and June 18, 2026 about an important December 7, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline in a securities class action lawsuit. The lawsuit alleges that Ensign made false statements regarding its business practices, including systematic neglect of elderly residents, fraudulent Medicaid/Medicare claims, falsification of nursing assistant hours, and illegal licensing schemes.

items.title: GlobalFoundries: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: GlobalFoundries reported record gross margins of 31.4% in Q3 2026, driven by a strategic shift away from lower-margin mobile devices toward high-growth optical networking and automotive silicon. The company expects silicon photonics revenue to hit $1 billion annualized run rate by end of 2027 (one year ahead of schedule) and plans to triple capacity in this segment. Notably, GFS is funding expansion through customer prepayments and government grants rather than heavy upfront capital spending, with planned 2027 net capex of approximately $4 billion. Over two-thirds of Q3 revenue now comes from non-mobile applications, demonstrating successful diversification.

items.title: INTC INVESTOR ALERT: Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd LLP Files Class Action Lawsuit Against Intel Corporation and Announces Opportunity for Investors with Substantial Losses to Lead the Intel Class Action Lawsuit
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Intel Corporation alleging that executives made materially false and misleading statements about the company's business performance during July-October 2026. The suit claims Intel failed to disclose a significant slowdown in PC market demand, excess inventory at partners, and substrate supply constraints that offset AI-related gains. Intel's stock fell nearly 30% after revealing Q3 2026 CCPG revenue declined 9% sequentially and providing weak Q4 guidance.

items.title: Why Intel Stock Slumped Today
items.summary: Intel stock fell nearly 3% on Friday amid concerns about leadership changes at Nvidia. The decline reflects uncertainty about Nvidia's new interim CEO Colette Kress replacing Jensen Huang, and potential impacts on Nvidia's $13 billion Intel shareholding and their collaborative x86 CPU development. Investors are cautious until the situation clarifies.

items.title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 13: CoreWeave Falls Over 6% on AI-Cloud Selling and Reported $4 Billion Loan Talks
items.summary: CoreWeave shares fell 6.13% on November 13, 2026, as investors weighed concerns about the company's $4 billion loan pursuits against its strong 168% revenue growth. The decline was triggered by uncertainty following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and worries about CoreWeave's escalating debt burden exceeding $40 billion. Despite impressive Q3 results and doubled 2026 revenue guidance, debt and leverage concerns remain central to investor sentiment.

items.title: NVDA CLASS ACTION UPDATE: Rosen Law Firm Expands Class Period to Include More NVIDIA Corporation Investors in Securities Class Action First Filed by the Firm - NVDA
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has expanded a securities class action lawsuit against NVIDIA Corporation, now covering investors who purchased securities between December 19, 2024 and November 12, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that NVIDIA made false and misleading statements regarding CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy connected to Megaspeed (a company suspected of helping China evade export controls), undisclosed affairs with subordinate employees, and the company's relationship with Megaspeed. The firm claims these omissions posed material risks to NVIDIA's reputation and business prospects.

items.title: Bullfrog AI Holdings Inc. (BFRG) Reports Q3 Loss, Lags Revenue Estimates
items.summary: Bullfrog AI Holdings Inc. (BFRG) reported a Q3 loss of $0.11 per share, missing consensus estimates of $0.09 loss by 22.22%. Revenue came in at $0.06 million, missing estimates by 71.1%. The stock has declined 37.4% year-to-date and received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, expected to perform in line with the market.

items.title: SpaceX Expects to Spend $35 Billion to $40 Billion This Quarter. Here's Who Sells the Power and Cooling.
items.summary: SpaceX plans to spend $35-40 billion in Q4 2026, primarily on Nvidia GPUs for its data centers. The company is building power generation and cooling infrastructure at Starbase, creating opportunities for suppliers like GE Vernova, Caterpillar, Trane, and Vertiv to benefit from the massive capital expenditure and broader data center market growth.

items.title: Applied Materials: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Applied Materials reported record fiscal 2026 revenue of $34.4 billion, growing 21% year-over-year, driven by AI infrastructure demand. The company plans to double systems output by 2028 and has achieved 14 consecutive quarters of gross margin expansion, positioning it to outgrow the broader wafer fab equipment market.
