items.title: AMD or Intel: 1 Chip Stock Is the Clear Winner
items.summary: AMD emerges as the superior investment choice compared to Intel, demonstrating stronger financial results with 45% revenue growth versus Intel's 21%, higher gross margins (54% vs 40%), and faster data center segment growth (97% vs 78%). AMD's better execution in outsourced manufacturing, stronger positioning for agentic AI demand, and more reasonable valuation (30.7x forward earnings vs Intel's 34.4x) make it the clear winner.

items.title: Why Sandisk Stock Is Falling Today
items.summary: Sandisk stock fell 8.2% on November 13, 2026, as a broader sell-off in AI hardware stocks spread following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation due to personal scandals involving alleged affairs and national security concerns. Despite Sandisk reporting strong fiscal Q1 results with $11 billion in sales (up 378% year-over-year) and 85.1% gross margins, investors worry the memory shortage could reverse as supply catches up or AI innovations reduce demand for expensive memory.

items.title: AMAT Q4 Earnings Call Highlights AI Demand and 2027 Growth Outlook
items.summary: Applied Materials (AMAT) projects wafer fab equipment spending to rise over 30% in 2027, driven by AI-related semiconductor demand. The company plans to double systems output by 2028 and expects Q1 FY2027 revenues of $11.1 billion with 58% year-over-year growth. Management identified advanced packaging, DRAM, and foundry-logic as key growth drivers, though supply-chain bottlenecks and cleanroom availability remain constraints.

items.title: JPMorgan Stock Slid After Reports That Senate Democrats Plan a New Investigation Into Jamie Dimon's Bank Over Its Jeffrey Epstein Relationship. Here's Why That Political Risk Could Weigh on JPM Shares.
items.summary: JPMorgan Chase's stock declined following reports that Senate Democrats plan to investigate the bank's historical ties to Jeffrey Epstein. Epstein banked at JPMorgan from 1998-2013, with the bank processing over $1 billion in transactions and generating $8 million in fees. A former executive exchanged over 1,200 emails with Epstein despite red flags. While the bank settled a 2023 class action lawsuit for $290 million with no admission of wrongdoing, new investigations could lead to additional fines, regulatory orders, increased compliance costs, or reputational damage, potentially weighing on the stock in the near term.

items.title: SHAREHOLDER ALERT: Bronstein Gewirtz & Grossman, LLC Announces Class Action Against NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ: NVDA) — Investors Who Suffered Losses Are Encouraged to Contact the Firm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against NVIDIA Corporation alleging that company executives made false and misleading statements regarding relationships with a company suspected of helping China evade export controls. The lawsuit covers investors who purchased NVIDIA securities between October 9, 2025 and November 8, 2026, with a lead plaintiff deadline of January 8, 2027.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges AppLovin Corporation Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against AppLovin Corporation alleging securities fraud. The complaint claims that between February 12, 2026 and August 5, 2026, AppLovin made false and misleading statements regarding its generative AI video creative feature, overstating AI model improvements and the benefits of its 'virtuous cycle' value proposition. Investors who purchased AppLovin securities during this period are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of November 16, 2026.

items.title: Coherent's Margin Expansion Steals the Spotlight in Q1 FY27
items.summary: Coherent Corp. (COHR) demonstrated notable profitability improvements in Q1 FY27, with non-GAAP gross margin expanding 184 basis points to 40.6% and operating margin increasing 368 basis points to 23.2%. Non-GAAP EPS surged 80% year-over-year to $2.09, driven by stronger operational execution and improved cost efficiency. The stock has gained 61% over the past year and currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

items.title: TE Connectivity: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: TE Connectivity reported strong Q4 2026 results with $2.6 billion in full-year sales growth. The company expects over $1 billion in new Digital Data Networks revenue in 2027 driven by AI data centers, sees $500 content opportunity per humanoid robot unit, and achieved 100% free cash flow conversion while expanding capital investments. A book-to-bill ratio of 1.14 and strong backlog position the company for double-digit top-line expansion in fiscal 2027.

items.title: Is Realty Income Stock a Smart Monthly Dividend Bet Heading Into 2027?
items.summary: Realty Income (O) offers an attractive 5.5% dividend yield with 137 consecutive dividend increases and strong portfolio fundamentals including 98.8% occupancy. However, persistent inflation, potential Fed rate hikes, refinancing pressures, and moderate rental growth could limit earnings expansion and valuation upside into 2027. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, suggesting investors maintain positions while monitoring dividend coverage and financing costs.

items.title: SoFi vs. Upstart: Which Fintech Stock is the Better Buy Right Now?
items.summary: SoFi Technologies and Upstart Holdings represent different fintech approaches. SoFi operates as a digital bank with deposits, loans, and diversified revenue streams, while Upstart focuses on AI-driven lending partnerships. SoFi shares fell 14.5% versus Upstart's 37.1% decline over three months. SoFi trades at 3.27X forward P/S (below its median) with stronger growth prospects, while Upstart at 1.12X P/S faces headwinds from worsening borrower conditions and reduced guidance.

items.title: ARM Stock Gains 4% Since Q2 Earnings: Is it a Buy or Hold Now?
items.summary: Arm Holdings reported Q2 fiscal 2027 revenues of $1.44 billion, beating consensus estimates, with strong licensing growth and upbeat Q3 guidance. The company targets up to $2 billion in cumulative AGI CPU revenues through fiscal 2028. However, weak quarterly cash flow (down 73% YoY), uneven royalty growth, and lower silicon margins (30-40% vs. traditional licensing margins) warrant caution. The stock maintains a Hold rating despite strong AI infrastructure tailwinds.

items.title: PLTR's Rule of 40 Hits 158%: Can This Momentum Continue?
items.summary: Palantir Technologies (PLTR) achieved a Rule of 40 score of 158% in Q3 2026, up from 81% in Q4 2024, driven by 96% year-over-year revenue growth and a 62% adjusted operating margin. U.S. commercial revenues surged 148% to $984 million while government revenues climbed 96%, supported by expanding AI Platform adoption. The company generated $1.22 billion in free cash flow with a 53% margin, though elevated investor expectations and valuation multiples present risks.

items.title: NU Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Credit Growth and Global Expansion
items.summary: Nu Holdings (NU) reported Q3 earnings of $0.22 per share with revenues of $5.82 billion, beating consensus estimates. The company's credit portfolio grew 33% to $41.6 billion with improved lending margins at 12.7%. NU raised its 2026 efficiency outlook to 19%-19.5% and is expanding operations in Mexico, Colombia, and the U.S., while maintaining disciplined credit growth and conservative underwriting standards.

items.title: Block's Square Expands Agentic Platform With Squaremates & New AI Tools
items.summary: Block, Inc.'s Square has launched Squaremates, an AI-powered agentic platform that automates complex business tasks for sellers including marketing, labor cost analysis, staffing optimization, and inventory management. The expansion includes new MCP and CLI tools enabling third-party AI integrations and custom applications. Square also introduced a voice-enabled kiosk and released over 180 features in 2026, with Q3 gross payment volume increasing 14% year-over-year to $76.4 billion.

items.title: You Can Do Better Than Tesla: 3 Industrial Stocks With More Upside
items.summary: The article argues that three industrial stocks—Caterpillar, Lockheed Martin, and GE Vernova—offer better investment opportunities than Tesla. These companies benefit from AI-driven electricity demand and defense spending, with record order backlogs stretching years into the future. Caterpillar's power generation revenue surged 75%, Lockheed Martin's backlog reached $292 billion, and GE Vernova's backlog hit $197 billion, while Tesla faces margin pressures and a softening EV market.

items.title: Innventure: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Innventure announced a strategic pivot focused on cost reduction and debt restructuring. The company cut parent staff by 62% (from 40 to 15 employees), suspended new development, and stopped funding its operating subsidiaries. Each subsidiary—including liquid-cooling business Accelsius, flexible-packaging developer AeroFlexx, and waste-conversion unit Refinity—must now secure external capital independently. Management hired RBC Capital Markets to evaluate all options including debt restructuring and potential asset monetization.

items.title: SHAREHOLDER ALERT: Bronstein Gewirtz & Grossman, LLC Announces Class Action Against Lululemon Athletica Inc. (NASDAQ: LULU) — Investors Who Suffered Losses Are Encouraged to Contact the Firm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Lululemon Athletica (NASDAQ: LULU) alleging that the company failed to disclose deteriorating store traffic and demand due to negative media commentary and weak product launches. The complaint claims defendants made materially false statements about the company's financial guidance and business strength, particularly in North America and Mainland China. Investors who purchased LULU securities between March 18, 2026 and September 3, 2026 may be eligible to recover losses, with a lead plaintiff deadline of January 4, 2027.

items.title: Costco Hits All-Time High Amid $4 Billion Buyback, Special Dividend
items.summary: Costco declared a record $30 per share special dividend ($13.3 billion) while reauthorizing a $4 billion buyback program through 2030. The company's restrained buyback usage suggests management views shares as fairly valued rather than cheap. Investors should focus on December 10th earnings results, where consensus expects $4.87 per share (up 12% YoY), though headline comparable sales growth of 11.1% masks a more modest 7.3% when excluding gasoline and FX impacts.

items.title: AECOM Q4 Earnings Ahead: What Should Investors Expect?
items.summary: AECOM is expected to report Q4 fiscal 2026 results on Nov. 16 with adjusted EPS projected at $1.59 (up 16.9%) but revenues expected to decline 1.9%. The company benefits from strong infrastructure demand and a $27.81 billion backlog (up 12%), with AI adoption supporting efficiency. Recent construction sector peers showed mixed results: Martin Marietta reported strong earnings with record volumes, CRH missed expectations and cut guidance, while MasTec exceeded estimates with robust backlog.

items.title: VIAV's Q1 Beat and Q2 Outlook Highlight Data Center Momentum Ahead
items.summary: Viavi Solutions (VIAV) delivered robust fiscal Q1 2027 results with revenues surging 56.9% to $469.3 million and earnings jumping 213.3%, beating consensus estimates. The company projects Q2 revenues of $505-$515 million with continued strength from data-center demand, 1.6T optics, and semiconductor testing. Operating margins expanded significantly to 29%, supported by the Spirent acquisition and operating leverage.

items.title: RITM vs. BX: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
items.summary: A comparison of Rithm (RITM) and Blackstone Inc. (BX) reveals that Rithm offers superior value for investors. RITM has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with a forward P/E of 3.87 and PEG ratio of 0.55, earning a Value grade of B. BX has a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) with a forward P/E of 20.13 and PEG ratio of 1.51, receiving a Value grade of D. Based on valuation metrics and earnings outlook, RITM is positioned as the better value opportunity.

items.title: PNC Financial Gains 10% in the 6 Months: What's Ahead for Investors?
items.summary: PNC Financial shares gained 10% over six months, outperforming peers through balance-sheet expansion, branch growth plans, and strategic acquisitions. The company raised its 2026 loan growth outlook to 13.5% and plans 370+ branches by 2031. However, rising operating expenses and heavy commercial loan concentration pose risks. PNC trades at an attractive 10.9X forward P/E with a 3.46% dividend yield, but investors may want to wait for clarity on expense trends before entering.

items.title: SO Q3 Earnings Beat on Data Center Demand, Outlook Raised
items.summary: Southern Company reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.94, up 21.3% year-over-year and beating estimates, with revenues climbing 13% to $8.84 billion. The company benefited from strong electricity demand, particularly from data centers (up 59%), and signed 4 GW of additional large-load contracts, bringing total contracted demand to 21 GW. Southern raised its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $4.70 and expanded its capital investment plan to approximately $85 billion through 2030.

items.title: This Video Game Publisher Has a Huge Catalyst Looming
items.summary: Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) is positioned for significant growth with Grand Theft Auto VI launching on November 19th. The company's latest quarterly results showed weakness with declining revenue, but management reaffirmed strong FY27 guidance of $8.0-$8.2 billion (roughly 20% growth), with GTA 6 as the primary driver. The unprecedented preorder activity and the decade-long success of GTA 5 (230 million copies sold) suggest strong long-term revenue potential through both initial sales and recurring GTA Online monetization.

items.title: TSMC’s Terrific Growth Clearly Shows That the Chip Sell-Off Is Overdone. Here Are the Best Stocks to Buy Hand Over Fist
items.summary: Despite a 17% decline in the semiconductor sector since early October, TSMC's October sales surged nearly 60% year-over-year, demonstrating that the chip sell-off is overdone. The company's accelerating growth is driven by robust AI infrastructure investments and agentic AI adoption. TSMC plans to increase capital expenditure to $60-64 billion in 2026, significantly benefiting equipment suppliers like ASML. Both TSMC and ASML are trading at attractive valuations and are well-positioned to capitalize on the AI-fueled chip boom.

items.title: Domino's Strong Order Trends vs. Weak Ticket Growth: What Lies Ahead?
items.summary: Domino's Pizza reported Q3 2026 U.S. same-store sales growth of 0.3%, driven by strong order count increases that offset declining average ticket sizes due to consumer spending pressures. The company is implementing value promotions and new products like The Domino to boost ticket growth, while expecting continued order momentum in Q4 but sales near the lower end of guidance. Domino's shares have outperformed the broader market, trading at a lower valuation than industry peers.

items.title: CBRS Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Rise on Strong Cloud Growth
items.summary: Cerebras Systems (CBRS) reported Q3 2026 earnings of 13 cents per share, beating estimates, with revenues surging 70% year-over-year to $230.87 million. Cloud revenues soared 272% to $144.91 million driven by AI inference demand and higher pricing. The company secured partnerships with Oracle and Microsoft, raised 2026 revenue guidance to $940-$960 million, and expects to triple revenues in 2027 with expanding data center capacity.

items.title: Cisco: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Cisco reported record Q1 FY2027 revenue of $18.5 billion, up 24% year-over-year, with AI infrastructure revenue projected to reach $9 billion in FY2027, more than double FY2026 levels. The company achieved operating leverage by reducing headcount while expanding revenue, expecting a 19% increase in revenue per employee. Management highlighted a multiyear networking super cycle driven by hyperscaler demand and enterprise modernization across data centers and campus networks.

items.title: Cisco's Q1 Earnings Beat Estimates, Strong Networking Aids Revenues
items.summary: Cisco Systems reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $1.40 per share, up 40% year-over-year, with revenues surging 24% to $18.52 billion. Networking revenues jumped 43%, driven by AI infrastructure growth and strong campus networking demand. The company raised its fiscal 2027 hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenue guidance to $9 billion from $7.5 billion and increased full-year revenue outlook to $74.8-$75.8 billion, reflecting sustained customer demand and broad-based growth.

items.title: NBIS Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Expansion Plans and Funding
items.summary: Nebius Group (NBIS) reported strong Q3 2026 earnings with 571% year-over-year revenue growth to $980.8M, beating estimates. The company targets $12-13B in 2027 revenues with pretax breakeven expected in Q4 2027. Management plans $40-45B in capex for 2027, with 75-85% funded through customer prepayments and asset-backed financing. Despite facility deployment delays, the company sees improving contract economics with customer prepayments now exceeding 100% of new capacity capex.

items.title: Corteva Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Brazil Woes and Outlook Cut
items.summary: Corteva reported Q3 2026 earnings that missed expectations with adjusted EPS of 6 cents versus 9 cents consensus and revenues of $1.52 billion versus $1.77 billion expected. The company significantly reduced full-year EBITDA guidance to $1.1-$1.13 billion from $1.3 billion due to severe conditions in Brazil, including $250 million in excess channel inventory, pricing pressure, and a 31% decline in Latin American organic sales. Management is implementing cost reduction initiatives and expects recovery in 2027 supported by inventory normalization and new product growth.

items.title: Cisco Q1 Earnings Call Highlights AI Growth and Higher Outlook
items.summary: Cisco raised its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $74.8B-$75.8B with non-GAAP EPS of $5.47-$5.53, driven by accelerating hyperscaler AI infrastructure demand and broad-based networking momentum. The company increased its hyperscaler AI revenue target to $9B from $7.5B, with networking orders up 28% and product orders up 21%. However, gross margin declined 250 basis points to 65.6% due to higher hardware exposure and rising memory costs.

items.title: AMAT Q4 Earnings Beat on Record Semiconductor Systems Sales
items.summary: Applied Materials (AMAT) reported Q4 fiscal 2026 earnings of $4.16 per share, up 92% year-over-year, with record revenues of $10.41 billion, up 53%. The company expects continued growth with Q1 FY27 revenue guidance of $11.1 billion and earnings of $4.35 per share, driven by robust demand for advanced chipmaking equipment and AI-related memory investments.

items.title: GridAI Technologies Signs Definitive Agreement to Acquire Pronghorn Resources, Establishing Major Wyoming Owned-Natural Gas and Multi-Gigawatt AI Power Infrastructure Platform Targeting Initial Power Delivery in 2027
items.summary: GridAI Technologies (Nasdaq: GRDX) announced a definitive agreement to acquire Pronghorn Resources, a Wyoming-based natural gas producer with ~100 MMcf/day production and 450+ miles of owned pipelines. The acquisition establishes a vertically integrated energy and AI infrastructure platform targeting 300 MW initial power delivery in 2027 to support hyperscale data center development. GridAI also acquired exclusive Wyoming rights for 1st American Nuclear Co.'s EAGL-1 240 MWe SMR platform.

items.title: Wells Fargo Eyes $50B NII in 2026: What's Fuelling the Optimism?
items.summary: Wells Fargo reaffirms its $50 billion net interest income (NII) target for 2026, with Q4 NII expected near $13 billion. The bank's NII grew 5.1% year-over-year to $36.93 billion in the first nine months of 2026, driven by expanding loan balances (up 11%), growing deposits (up 9%), and fixed-rate asset repricing. The removal of the asset cap and mid-single-digit growth projections for loans and deposits support the outlook.

items.title: Wall Street Divided on S&P 500: Which ETFs Could Benefit in 2027?
items.summary: Wall Street strategists are divided on the S&P 500's 2027 outlook. UBS forecasts the index reaching 8,900 (17.22% upside) driven by earnings growth, while Bank of America warns that crowded equity positioning, AI valuation risks, and potential outflows could limit gains. The divergence highlights key risks including elevated valuations, geopolitical uncertainty, and concentration in mega-cap tech stocks.

items.title: Home Depot Pre-Q3 Earnings: Should You Buy or Stay Cautious?
items.summary: Home Depot is expected to report Q3 fiscal 2026 results on November 17 with projected revenue growth of 3.3% to $42.7B and EPS growth of 3.5%. While the company benefits from strong Pro sales, digital expansion, and smaller home improvement projects, near-term challenges include weak housing turnover, margin pressures from tariffs and operating costs, and a premium valuation of 22.27X forward P/E.

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway’s Greg Abel Bought Back a Record $9.6 Billion of Stock Last Quarter. Here’s Why That Pace Might Not Continue.
items.summary: Greg Abel, Berkshire Hathaway's new CEO, executed a record $9.6 billion in share buybacks during Q3 2026, surpassing Warren Buffett's previous quarterly record. However, the pace is likely to slow significantly as Berkshire's stock price has climbed above key valuation thresholds. With the price-to-book ratio now at 1.6 (compared to Buffett's previous buyback threshold of 1.5), Abel is unlikely to continue aggressive repurchases unless the stock price pulls back, adhering to Buffett's principle that buybacks should only occur at discounts to intrinsic value.

items.title: NVIDIA Leadership Crisis Opens Door for Chip Rivals? ETFs in Focus
items.summary: Following Jensen Huang's resignation as NVIDIA CEO due to personal scandals, investors are rotating toward competing semiconductor companies including AMD, Broadcom, and TSMC. While NVIDIA shares fell 4.3%, AMD and Broadcom gained 5.9% and 5.5% respectively. Despite the management uncertainty, the broader AI investment cycle remains strong, though growing competition could eventually commoditize AI capabilities and pressure chip prices.

items.title: What's Wrong With Amazon.com (AMZN) Stock, and Is It a Buy in November?
items.summary: Amazon stock has gained 9% over the past year, below its historical averages, but the company remains fundamentally strong with 12% revenue growth, record operating margins of 13.9%, and AWS cloud revenue surging 39% year-over-year. While concerns exist around slowing e-commerce growth, heavy AI capital expenditures, and shrinking free cash flow, the author recommends Amazon as a buy for long-term investors given its reasonable forward P/E ratio of 25 (below its five-year average of 38) and strong growth metrics.

items.title: What's Going on With Intel Stock?
items.summary: Intel stock has declined more than 50% from its all-time highs. The article discusses Intel's recent stock performance struggles, including a 29% plunge, though the CEO purchased $9.7 million in stock following the decline. Intel shares showed some recovery as part of a broader chip rally driven by AI infrastructure demand.

items.title: Can Nebius Sustain 571% Revenue Growth Beyond Its Q3 AI Cloud Boom?
items.summary: Nebius Group (NBIS) delivered impressive Q3 2026 results with revenues surging 571% year-over-year to $980.8 million, driven by AI infrastructure demand and capacity additions. The company secured over $12 billion in customer commitments with contract pricing exceeding $25 million per megawatt. While profitability improved significantly with adjusted EBITDA reaching $465.8 million, deployment delays and substantial capital requirements of $40-45 billion for 2027 remain key challenges. NBIS targets $12-13 billion in 2027 revenues.

items.title: Macy's Extends Its AI Shopping Assistant From Online to In-Store Teams
items.summary: Macy's has expanded its Ask Macy's AI shopping assistant to in-store associates to enhance customer engagement and personalized shopping. Digital sales accounted for 31% of total sales in Q2 2026, with comparable sales rising 1.1% at the Macy's nameplate and 11.3% at Bloomingdale's. The company raised its fiscal 2026 sales outlook to $21.68-$21.83 billion, supported by improved inventory allocation through AI forecasting and faster fulfillment times.

items.title: NBIS Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on AI Cloud Growth, Asset-Light Gains
items.summary: Nebius Group (NBIS) reported Q3 2026 earnings of 30 cents per share, beating estimates, with revenues surging 571% to $980.8M driven by AI Cloud growth of 643%. The company expanded EBITDA margins to 47.5% through stronger pricing and asset-light partnerships. Management expects 2027 to be the cycle's trough with recovery anticipated in 2028 driven by new product launches.

The company is investing heavily in AI infrastructure and custom chips, though this has resulted in negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion over the past 12 months.

PhotonLink platform revenues are expected to reach $250M by end of 2027. However, the company faces significant capex spending ($776M) to meet booked demand through 2027.

items.title: These 6 Data Software Stocks Help Companies Put AI to Work
items.summary: Six data software companies—Snowflake, Datadog, MongoDB, Cloudflare, Elastic, and Palantir—are benefiting from AI adoption with revenue growth ranging from 15% to 96%. Specialty testing is growing 3x faster than the broader diagnostics market, and tuck-in acquisitions from BioReference, Myriad Genetics' prenatal business, and Millennium Health are expected to be accretive to earnings in year one.

items.summary: Cisco Systems reported record fiscal Q1 results with adjusted EPS of $1.40 (up 40% YoY) and revenue of $18.52 billion (up 24% YoY), driven by strong AI infrastructure and networking demand. The company raised its FY27 revenue guidance to $74.8-$75.8 billion and adjusted EPS guidance to $5.47-$5.53, with hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenue expected to exceed $9 billion. items.summary: The Nasdaq achieved a bullish follow-through day signal with a 2.31% gain on heavy volume, signaling renewed institutional appetite for AI stocks. Despite NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's resignation due to personal scandal, the market showed resilience with NVIDIA shares recovering losses. Neocloud providers CoreWeave and Nebius reported exceptional revenue growth, while Micron regained its 200-day moving average. items.summary: Broadcom stock surged 5.49% following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation due to personal conduct issues. The conglomerate's cash hoard grew to over $377 billion, and its diverse revenue streams make it a unique hedge against AI-dependent investments.

items.title: ASUS Expands Access to Local AI Across DIY PCs, Gaming Systems, Creator Workstations, and Professional Desktops
items.summary: ASUS launched the Agent Computer initiative to democratize AI access across its product ecosystem, offering AI-ready hardware ranging from DIY PC builds to enterprise supercomputers, alongside software solutions like ASUS Zenni Claw and Multi-LM Tuner. The miss was driven by rapid price declines in agricultural chemicals, particularly in Latin America where sales fell 28% year-over-year. Management expects challenging market conditions ahead, especially in Brazil, though full-year guidance remains between $0.76-$0.80 per share on an adjusted basis—below Wall Street's GAAP expectations of $0.82.

items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Webull Corporation (NASDAQ: BULL) alleging that the company made false and misleading statements about its operations. The complaint claims Webull misrepresented its independence from China, stating that its software development, data pipelines, and core engineering actually depend on PRC-based personnel and infrastructure, contrary to claims that principal operations were U.S.-based. The lead plaintiff deadline is December 7, 2026.

However, the company trimmed its adjusted EBITDA outlook to at least $2.5 million from over $4 million due to additional operating investments. The company faces margin pressures from product mix and freight costs but expects improvement through higher-margin pouch cell shipments and a shift to ocean freight in 2027.

items.title: MRNA Stock Up 3% Since Q3 Earnings Release: How to Play the Stock?
items.summary: Moderna shares gained 3% following better-than-expected Q3 2026 earnings and raised full-year revenue guidance to 15-25% growth, driven by stronger international COVID-19 vaccine sales. The company's oncology pipeline, particularly its personalized cancer therapy intismeran developed with Merck, showed promising phase III results with a 42% reduction in recurrence or death risk. Despite premium valuation and ongoing cash burn concerns, Moderna maintains a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating, supported by expanding respiratory vaccine portfolio and oncology opportunities.

items.title: Few S&P 500 Stocks Yield Over 5%. Here's My Top Pick to Buy Now.
items.summary: With Treasury yields rising above 5%, dividend stocks are becoming less attractive. However, UPS stands out as one of only ~20 S&P 500 stocks offering yields over 5% at 5.8%. Trading at 15x adjusted EPS with 16 consecutive years of dividend increases, UPS offers a reliable income play for conservative investors.

items.title: Procter & Gamble (PG) Has Raised Its Dividend for 70 Straight Years. Here's Why I'd Buy Before 2027.
items.summary: Procter & Gamble is highlighted as a reliable dividend investment with 70 consecutive years of dividend increases and 136 years of continuous dividend payments. The company offers a 2.6% dividend yield with average annual growth of 4.6% over the past five years. With a strong portfolio of consumer staple brands and defensive characteristics during economic downturns, PG is positioned as a stable investment option, though shares are reasonably but not cheaply priced at a forward P/E ratio of 24.

items.title: Advanced Micro Devices vs. Marvell Technology: Which Artificial Intelligence Stock Is a Better Buy Going into 2027?
items.summary: The article compares AMD and Marvell Technology as AI semiconductor investments through 2027. While AMD shows strong growth with major partnerships (Meta, OpenAI) and $34.6B revenue, Marvell is recommended as the better value due to lower valuation multiples, higher profit margins (32.6% vs 12.5%), and aggressive growth guidance ($20B revenue by FY2028, $70-90B by FY2031). Marvell's acquisition of Lumentum strengthens its optical components capabilities for AI infrastructure.

items.title: LEN INVESTOR ALERT: Lennar Corporation Investors with Substantial Losses May Seek to Lead the Lennar Class Action Lawsuit – RGRD Law
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Lennar Corporation alleging securities fraud related to improper capitalization of costs, the Millrose spin-off being used to artificially inflate financial performance, and undisclosed related-party transactions. The lawsuit covers stock purchases between February 7, 2025 and October 2, 2026, with significant stock price declines following disclosure of accounting irregularities and a short-seller report revealing Millrose purchased over 700 homes from Lennar at above-market rates.

items.title: Dell Technologies vs. Taiwan Semiconductor: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
items.summary: The article compares Dell Technologies and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing as AI investment opportunities. Dell trades at a lower valuation (Forward P/E 12.9x vs TSM's 23.9x) and is expected to grow AI server sales to $60 billion in FY2027. TSM maintains a near-monopoly on advanced chip manufacturing with a 44.6% net margin. The author recommends Dell as the better buy for 2027 due to its attractive valuation metrics, despite both companies being strong AI-driven growth plays.

items.title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 11: Stock Market Today, Nov. 11: Nasdaq Surges as CoreWeave's 25% Rally Reignites the AI Trade
items.summary: Wall Street staged a strong recovery on November 11 as AI enthusiasm returned, lifting technology and semiconductor stocks. The Nasdaq climbed 1.60% to 25,466, while the S&P 500 gained 1.29% to 7,618. CoreWeave surged 24.71% on record earnings and improved revenue outlook, while Micron Technology and Oracle also posted significant gains. However, underlying economic concerns about inflation and elevated valuations persist.

items.title: GE HealthCare: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: GE HealthCare raised its full-year 2026 organic revenue guidance to 4% and reported 6.2% organic revenue growth in Q3 2026. The company's equipment backlog grew 12% year-over-year to $23.7 billion. Key strengths include recurring revenue from its Pharmaceutical Diagnostics division, operational improvements through the Heartbeat operating system, and multiyear supply agreements for memory chips that provide manufacturing resilience amid industry shortages.

items.title: Costco Just Declared a $30 Special Dividend. Is It Reason Enough to Buy the Stock Before Nov. 24?
items.summary: Costco announced a $30-per-share special dividend (its largest ever at $13.3 billion total) payable December 4 to shareholders of record by November 24. While the company's fundamentals are strong and it has a track record of special dividends, the stock trades at a premium 51.4 P/E ratio, making it expensive compared to peers. The author suggests investors should only buy if they believe in long-term ownership, not purely for the dividend.

items.title: Johnson & Johnson vs. Eli Lilly: Which Healthcare Giant's Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
items.summary: The article compares two pharmaceutical giants for 2027 investment. Johnson & Johnson offers stability with a 6% revenue growth, lower P/E ratio of 42.59, and strong free cash flow of $19.7B, but faces patent expirations and litigation risks. Eli Lilly demonstrates explosive 44.7% revenue growth driven by GLP-1 drugs like Mounjaro and Zepbound, commanding a premium valuation (P/E 47.05), with significant future growth potential but concentrated revenue dependency.

items.title: Cloudforce Named 2026 Microsoft Education Partner of the Year, the First Company Ever to Win the Award Twice
items.summary: Cloudforce has won the Microsoft Education Partner of the Year Award for 2026, becoming the first company to win the award twice consecutively. The company's nebulaONE AI platform is now used by over 100 universities and has more than doubled its annual recurring revenue in the past 12 months, positioning it as the leading AI platform for higher education worldwide.

items.title: Johnson & Johnson Sees a Path to Double-Digit Growth by 2030. Is the Dividend King a Buy?
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson is positioned to achieve double-digit sales growth by 2030 following its consumer health spinoff. Despite facing a major patent cliff with Stelara losing exclusivity in 2025, the company's new drug launches (Icotyde, Inlexzo, Lazcluze, Imaavy) with peak sales potential exceeding $5 billion each, combined with its robotic surgery device Ottava and strong dividend history as a Dividend King, make it an attractive investment for long-term income seekers.

items.title: SHAREHOLDER ALERT: Bronstein Gewirtz & Grossman, LLC Announces Class Action Against Bank of America Corporation (NYSE: BAC) — Investors Who Suffered Losses Are Encouraged to Contact the Firm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Bank of America Corporation alleging the bank made false and misleading statements regarding its Bank Secrecy Act and Anti-Money Laundering compliance program. The complaint claims BAC failed to properly monitor trillions of dollars in transactions and failed to adequately remediate compliance deficiencies documented in internal reports following a 2024 Consent Order. Investors who purchased BAC securities between August 1, 2025 and October 13, 2026 may be eligible to recover losses, with a lead plaintiff deadline of December 15, 2026.

items.title: Kaplan Fox Notifies The Ensign Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: ENSG) Investors of a Securities Class Action Lawsuit – Deadline is December 7, 2026
items.summary: Kaplan Fox has filed a securities class action lawsuit against The Ensign Group on behalf of investors who purchased securities between February 10, 2022 and June 18, 2026. The complaint alleges that Ensign's business model relies on systematic neglect of elderly patients, fraudulent Medicaid/Medicare claims, and falsification of records. Following a June 8, 2026 investigative report by Hunterbrook Media detailing these allegations, Ensign's stock fell 8.15% to $156.42 per share. The deadline to join the class action is December 7, 2026.

items.title: EMCOR Stock Plunges 17% in a Month: Buy the Low Now or Wait?
items.summary: EMCOR Group (EME) has raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $20.6-$21 billion and adjusted EPS guidance to $34.50-$35.50, driven by a record $18.57 billion backlog and 20.8% organic growth. Despite a 17.2% stock decline over the past month due to concerns about data-center regulatory restrictions and high borrowing costs, the company's diversified infrastructure exposure across healthcare, utilities, and institutional markets provides a cushion. Strong execution, improving margins, and strategic acquisitions support long-term growth prospects.

items.title: Realty Income's Dividend Growth: Can Strong AFFO Sustain It?
items.summary: Realty Income (O) increased its monthly dividend to 27.40 cents per share, its 137th hike since 1994. Q3 AFFO rose 3.7% to $1.12 per share with a 72.6% payout ratio. The REIT invested $2.6 billion at 6.8% yield and raised 2026 AFFO guidance to $4.45-$4.46. However, same-store rental revenue growth of only 1.1% suggests limited organic expansion, with future dividend growth dependent on external investments and capital deployment.

items.title: Why Advanced Micro Devices Stock Popped Today
items.summary: AMD stock surged 8.43% following CoreWeave's strong Q3 earnings beat and raised guidance for 2026, signaling increased capital spending on semiconductor chips. Additionally, a UBS report highlighted that server CPU shipments jumped 31% year-over-year in Q3, with AMD maintaining steady market share at 28.4% while Intel declined. UBS projects CPU sales could reach $210 billion by 2030, potentially generating $60 billion in revenue for AMD alone.

items.title: Ciena's $116M Free Cash Flow: Can Cash Generation Improve in FY27?
items.summary: Ciena Corporation generated $116M in Q3 free cash flow with revenues surging 37% to $1.67B and adjusted operating margin reaching a record 22.5%. The company expects fiscal 2027 revenues of $8.3-$8.4B with 30%+ growth, though near-term cash generation may face pressure from supply chain investments extending through 2029.

items.title: ServiceNow Drops 29% in a Month: Should You Hold or Fold the Stock?
items.summary: ServiceNow (NOW) shares dropped 29% in a month, underperforming the tech sector due to slowing cRPO growth guidance (18.5% vs 21%), rising infrastructure costs pressuring profitability, and increased debt from acquisitions. While AI net new ACV surged 65% with strong long-term potential, the company's premium valuation and near-term challenges warrant caution.

items.title: COHR Stock Gains 10% After Strong Q1 Earnings: Is it Still a Buy?
items.summary: Coherent Corp. (COHR) shares gained 10% following fiscal Q1 2027 earnings that beat expectations with adjusted EPS of $2.09 and record revenues of $2.37 billion. Datacenter revenues surged 85% year-over-year, driving 82% of total revenues, while gross margins expanded and operating efficiency improved. The company projects fiscal 2027 pro forma revenue growth exceeding 60% and expects quarterly revenues to reach $3 billion by end of fiscal 2027 and $4 billion in fiscal 2028, supported by strong AI infrastructure demand and a $20 billion five-year customer agreement.

items.title: CLS vs. SANM: Which Stock is Better Positioned for the AI Boom?
items.summary: Celestica and Sanmina, two major electronics manufacturing services providers, are competing for opportunities in the expanding AI and cloud computing market. Celestica demonstrates stronger near-term performance with 82.5% Q3 revenue growth, record 8.5% operating margins, and a 28.5% ROIC, earning a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). Sanmina is strengthening its AI exposure through the ZT Systems acquisition and vertically integrated capabilities but faces working capital challenges with $3.15 billion in inventory and lower profitability metrics, holding a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

items.title: NetApp's Q2 Gross Margin Guide: Is Another Sequential Dip Ahead?
items.summary: NetApp projects Q2 FY27 gross margin of 67-68%, down from 70.6% in Q1, driven by a higher product revenue mix and rising component costs. Despite strong 23% year-over-year revenue growth expected at $2.1 billion, the company faces margin pressures, though pricing gains are helping offset cost increases. For full FY27, NetApp forecasts gross margin of 68.1-69.1%.

items.title: Can General Mills' New Operating Model Drive Profitable Growth?
items.summary: General Mills announced a major restructuring effective January 1, 2027, consolidating operations into three segments: Cereal, Snacks & International; Meals & Baking Solutions; and Pet. The company will also establish a centralized commercial function to improve efficiency and decision-making. GIS targets $750 million in cost savings for fiscal 2027 and at least $3 billion by fiscal 2030, though recent performance showed flat organic sales and declining operating profit.

items.title: Can 3M Sustain Operating Margin Momentum Amid Sales Growth?
items.summary: 3M Company achieved solid Q3 2026 results with adjusted operating income rising 8.9% to $1.73 billion and operating margin expanding to 26.2%. Revenue grew 1% year-over-year to $6.6 billion, driven by strength in industrial, safety, semiconductor, and data center markets. The company expects 2026 EPS of $9.10-$9.15 with organic sales growth above 3.5% and an operating margin of 24.6%. Peer GE Aerospace saw margin contraction while Honeywell Technologies showed significant margin improvement.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges AST SpaceMobile, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against AST SpaceMobile, Inc. alleging securities fraud. The complaint claims the company made false statements about its capital requirements, competitive position in the satellite direct-to-cell market, and user adoption rates. The class period covers purchases between March 4, 2025 and July 15, 2026, with a lead plaintiff deadline of November 13, 2026.

items.title: Is Howmet Aerospace Stock a Buy After Q3 Earnings Beat & Raised Outlook?
items.summary: Howmet Aerospace (HWM) reported Q3 2026 earnings that surged 54% with revenues up 29%, driven by strong commercial and defense aerospace demand. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $10.29-$10.31 billion and adjusted EPS to $5.49-$5.51. While the company benefits from robust engine spare demand and healthy aircraft build rates, its premium valuation at 34.46X forward P/E remains a concern compared to industry peers.

items.title: Here's Why Bloom Energy Stock Popped Today
items.summary: Bloom Energy stock surged 15.32% following positive updates from the data center sector. CoreWeave reported strong Q3 results with overwhelming infrastructure demand, easing concerns about a slowdown in data center construction. Additionally, SoftBank's $3.7 billion loss on power generation equipment for data centers suggests potential increased demand for Bloom's fuel cell alternatives. The company maintains a positive order trajectory with record quarterly revenue and raised full-year guidance.

items.title: SoundHound's $120M Annual Cost Cuts: A Path to Profitability?
items.summary: SoundHound AI (SOUN) is pursuing $120 million in annualized cost savings following its LivePerson acquisition, with over $80 million already executed. The company targets positive adjusted EBITDA in H2 2027 despite widening Q3 losses. Cost reductions span merger synergies, cloud optimization, AI efficiencies, and strategic resource reallocation. However, integration risks and elevated AI infrastructure costs remain concerns.

items.title: Fortinet Raises 2026 Outlook After Strong Q3: Time to Hold the Stock?
items.summary: Fortinet raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $8.125-$8.215 billion following strong Q3 results with 20% revenue growth and 29% billings growth. While AI security launches and robust cash generation support the company, decelerating product growth, margin pressure, and premium valuation suggest investors should hold or wait for better entry points. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: GS' Capital Distribution Strategy: Can It Sustain Higher Payouts?
items.summary: Goldman Sachs increased its quarterly dividend by 11% to $5 per share following the Fed's 2026 stress test. The company returned $4.49 billion to shareholders in Q3 2026, including $3 billion in buybacks, and maintains $20 billion in remaining buyback capacity supported by $177 billion in cash. GS shares have outperformed the banking industry year-to-date, gaining 5.5% versus 0.6% industry growth.

items.title: Vertiv's Data Center Growth Fuels Revenue: Can It Beat APH and SMCI?
items.summary: Vertiv (VRT) reported Q3 2026 revenues of $4.31 billion, up 61% year-over-year, driven by strong demand for AI infrastructure and hyperscale data center solutions. However, the company faces increasing competition from Super Micro Computer and Amphenol. VRT stock trades at a premium valuation of 13.59X Price/Book versus the sector's 8.18X, though it has gained 19.9% year-to-date.

items.title: SK hynix Rides the AI Data Center Boom and HBM4 Ramp-Up
items.summary: SK hynix is well-positioned to capitalize on growing AI data center investments and rising demand for high-performance memory solutions. The company has begun mass production of HBM4 chips and expects them to surpass HBM3E in shipment volume and revenue by Q4 2026. With cloud providers expected to increase capex by 60%+ in 2027 and AI data center buildout growing at 40% CAGR through 2030, SKHY trades at a valuation discount (P/E of 3.51X vs. industry average of 9.47X) and currently holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: HAS Stock Up 29% in a Month: Time to Lock in Gains or Stay Invested?
items.summary: Hasbro (HAS) reported Q3 2026 revenues of $1.6 billion (+15% YoY) with adjusted EPS surging 73% to $2.90, driven by Wizards of the Coast's 31% revenue growth and Magic: The Gathering's 34% increase. The company raised its 2026 revenue outlook to 7-9% growth and doubled its share repurchase target to $400 million. HAS shares gained 28.6% over the past month, outperforming the broader market and industry peers.

items.title: TRGP Q3 Earnings Beat on Permian Growth and Higher Fees
items.summary: Targa Resources (TRGP) reported Q3 2026 earnings of $3.04 per share, beating estimates by 8.19%, with revenues up 34.9% to $5.6 billion. Record Permian inlet volumes and higher midstream fees drove adjusted EBITDA up 18% to $1.5B. The company raised its 2026 EBITDA outlook to at least $6B and increased its quarterly dividend by 25% to $1.25 per share, with plans for a 20% annualized dividend increase to $6 per share in 2027.

items.title: Costco's $30 Special Dividend Set to Boost Investor Confidence
items.summary: Costco announced a $30-per-share special dividend totaling $13.3 billion and renewed a $4 billion stock repurchase program, reflecting strong cash generation with fiscal 2026 cash reserves reaching $20.2 billion. While the stock has outperformed its industry by 25.6% year-to-date, its forward P/E ratio of 46.07 signals premium valuation that may limit near-term upside.

items.title: RKLB Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Neutron Demand and Launch Delays
items.summary: Rocket Lab reported Q3 revenues of $267.83M (73% YoY growth, beating estimates) but posted a wider-than-expected loss of 7 cents per share. The company secured $1B in new launch contracts, boosting backlog to $3.57B, with improved pricing power. However, Neutron's first launch shifted to 2027 due to manufacturing defects. The pending Iridium acquisition is fully financed with shareholder approval, though regulatory approval remains pending. Cash flow remains pressured despite positive GAAP operating cash flow of $7.2M.

items.title: AI Trade Comes Back Post-CoreWeave Numbers
items.summary: U.S. stock markets are open on Veterans Day with pre-market gains across major indices. Goldman Sachs projects a 25 basis-point Fed rate hike in March 2027, in addition to expected December hike. CoreWeave surged 15% after strong earnings beat, while NVIDIA faces ongoing investigations into CEO Jensen Huang. Wholesale inflation (PPI) expected to come in hot at +6.6% on Friday.

items.title: Here's Why Cardinal Health (CAH) is a Great Momentum Stock to Buy
items.summary: Cardinal Health (CAH) is highlighted as a momentum investment pick with a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) and Momentum Style Score of B. The stock has outperformed its industry with 8.48% weekly gains and 35.15% annual returns, while recent earnings estimate revisions have moved higher, supporting its bullish outlook.

items.title: CoreWeave Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Funding and Margin Gains
items.summary: CoreWeave (CRWV) raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $13-$13.3B following Q3 revenues of $3.66B that beat consensus estimates. The company reported improved operating margins at 10%, expects $9B in customer prepayments over three months, and identified nearly $10B in potential annualized GPU renewal revenues from 2027-2028. Management emphasized pricing strength with 25-35% increases implemented and expects to achieve positive adjusted net income in H1 2028.

items.title: Can UltiSynq Lead Boost Abbott's Cardiac Rhythm Management Business?
items.summary: Abbott (ABT) announced FDA and CE Mark approvals for its UltiSynq defibrillation lead, which delivers both pacing and defibrillation therapy. The ASCEND CSP IDE trial demonstrated a 98.5% successful implantation rate, 97.5% complication-free rate, and 100% successful defibrillation in 120 tested patients. The device received FDA breakthrough designation. Competitors Medtronic and Boston Scientific also reported positive clinical results for their respective cardiac devices.

items.title: 5 Great AI Infrastructure Stocks to Buy on a Dip
items.summary: The AI sector has experienced a recent market dip, but five infrastructure companies show strong fundamentals and improving earnings momentum. GE Vernova, Vertiv, ON Semiconductor, Comfort Systems USA, and SPX Technologies all benefit from accelerating AI data center demand, with expanding backlogs and raised guidance despite stock price declines over the past three months.

items.title: HPE or AGYS: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
items.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is identified as the superior value stock compared to Agilysys (AGYS) in the Computer-Integrated Systems sector. HPE holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with a Value grade of B, featuring a forward P/E of 10.22 and PEG ratio of 0.29, indicating stronger earnings outlook and better valuation metrics. AGYS, with a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) and Value grade of F, has a forward P/E of 48.65 and PEG ratio of 2.43, suggesting it is overvalued relative to growth prospects.

items.title: Dylanex Announces Q4 Inventory Preparation Guidance for Amazon Sellers Ahead of Holiday Shopping Season
items.summary: Dylanex, an FBA prep and fulfillment company, has released guidance for Amazon sellers to optimize Q4 inventory management during the holiday season. The company recommends five key strategies including checking inbound timing, ensuring proper product preparation, planning around restock limits, maintaining reserve inventory outside FBA, and managing inventory across multiple sales channels to avoid stock-outs and excess storage fees.

items.title: What You Actually Own When You Buy a Share of Berkshire Hathaway
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway is a conglomerate that owns approximately 70 private companies across insurance, railroads, construction, and consumer brands, alongside a $335 billion stock portfolio. Under new CEO Greg Abel, the company maintains Warren Buffett's value-investing philosophy and culture focused on long-term performance. Since 1965, Berkshire has delivered 19.7% average annual returns, nearly double the S&P 500's 10.5%, making it one of the most reliable stocks for investors.

items.title: VG Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Higher Outlook and AI Power Plans
items.summary: Venture Global (VG) raised its 2026 EBITDA guidance to $10-$10.3 billion from $8.7-$9.1 billion following a strong Q3 earnings beat. The company reported EPS of 96 cents versus 53 cents estimate and revenues of $4.76 billion. VG accelerated CP2's first LNG production target to July 2027 and increased 2026 cargo outlook to 509-518. Additionally, the company outlined plans to develop 5 GW of AI compute capacity by 2031 using existing power infrastructure, with initial capacity expected in late 2028 or early 2029.

items.title: ASTS Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Service Rollout and Launch Plans
items.summary: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) reported Q3 2026 earnings with plans to activate intermittent satellite broadband service by year-end 2026, targeting 45 satellites in orbit by mid-2027 and monthly production of six satellites by December. The company is advancing its Blacklift reusable rocket project and secured approximately $1 billion in nondilutive Japanese funding for the J-LEO program plus a $100 million U.S. Space Force contract. ASTS reaffirmed its 2026 revenue guidance of $150-200 million despite Q3 revenue missing consensus estimates.

items.title: Coinbase Global vs. Toast: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
items.summary: The article compares Coinbase Global and Toast as investment options for 2027. Coinbase operates as a crypto exchange with $7.2B in revenue and 17.6% net margin, while Toast provides restaurant software with $6.2B in revenue and 24.1% growth. Toast has a lower valuation (P/E 24.9 vs 53.8) and recently turned profitable. The author recommends Toast, citing skepticism about crypto's intrinsic value and concerns about Coinbase's heavy dependence on Bitcoin and Ethereum price movements.

items.title: Alphabet or CoreWeave: Which AI Stock Is Better to Buy in a Market Crash?
items.summary: The article compares Alphabet and CoreWeave as AI investment opportunities during a market crash. Alphabet is recommended as the safer choice due to its diversified revenue streams (Google Search, YouTube, Google Cloud) and strong financial foundation, while CoreWeave offers higher growth potential but carries greater financial risk due to massive capital expenditure requirements ($9.4B in Q2 2026) and dependence on continued financing.

items.title: 1 Unstoppable AI Stock to Buy Hand Over Fist Before the Next Leg Higher
items.summary: Iren, an AI data center company, has crashed 70% from its all-time high despite strengthening fundamentals. The company's AI cloud revenue nearly tripled sequentially to $200M, megawatt pricing has more than doubled to $22-40M per megawatt (vs. $9.7M previously), and it has a $20.3B revenue backlog with $1B in operating annual recurring revenue. With a 35-gigawatt development pipeline and strong financing through prepayments, Iren appears undervalued at current levels.

items.title: Tech Sell-Off: Two AI Stocks That Are Screaming Buys Right Now
items.summary: Following a tech sell-off triggered by concerns about AI regulation after Democratic election victories, the article identifies Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) and Broadcom as attractive buying opportunities. Both companies benefit from AI growth while maintaining diversified revenue streams beyond AI chips, with TSMC trading at 22x forward earnings and Broadcom at 16x forward earnings after recent declines.

items.title: INVESTOR ACTION NOTICE: Moore Law PLLC Encourages Investors in NVIDIA Corporation to Contact Law Firm
items.summary: Moore Law PLLC is investigating NVIDIA Corporation for allegedly making false and misleading statements regarding CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy connected to Megaspeed, a company suspected of helping China evade export controls. The investigation raises national security concerns about NVIDIA's business relationships. NVIDIA has hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation, and the FBI is also probing the matter. NVIDIA's stock has fallen significantly, losing approximately $500 billion in market value since November 6, 2026.

items.title: 1 Unstoppable Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock Poised to Join the $5 Trillion Club by 2029
items.summary: SpaceX's AI division generated $7.56 billion in Q3 revenue, surpassing its Starlink connectivity business. With a potential merger with Tesla under exploration, the combined entity could reach a $5 trillion valuation by 2029, requiring approximately 47% appreciation from their combined $3.4 trillion market value.

items.title: Is Nvidia Stock a Buy on the Spy Allegation Sell-Off?
items.summary: Nvidia shares dropped over 20% after CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with someone accused of being a Chinese spy. The company's board investigation found no compromise of secrets or national security. Despite the scandal, the article argues Nvidia remains an attractive AI infrastructure leader trading at a forward P/E of 11x fiscal 2028 estimates, with strong competitive advantages in GPU technology and strategic partnerships.

items.title: STLD Boosts Shareholder Returns With $3B Buyback Authorization
items.summary: Steel Dynamics (STLD) announced an additional $3 billion share repurchase program, effective immediately, demonstrating management confidence in the company's cash flow generation. Since 2017, STLD has repurchased $8.2 billion in shares and distributed $2.2 billion in dividends. The company maintains a low-cost operating model and disciplined capital allocation strategy while preserving investment-grade credit ratings.

items.title: Arista Networks: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Arista Networks reported Q3 2026 revenue of $3.66 billion, up 58.5% year-over-year, driven by surging AI infrastructure demand. The company forecasts fiscal 2027 revenue of $18.5 billion with 38-40% growth. Key strengths include its unified operating system architecture that minimizes security vulnerabilities, expansion of open Ethernet standards for AI deployments (projected to exceed 10 gigawatts by 2027), and accelerating enterprise campus growth expected to reach $2 billion in 2027.

items.title: Everest Group, Ltd. Notice of December 28, 2026 Application Deadline for Class Action Lawsuit - Contact Lewis Kahn, Esq. at Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC, Before Application Deadline
items.summary: A class action securities lawsuit has been filed against Everest Group, Ltd. for allegedly making false statements about insurance reserve adequacy. The company disclosed $478 million in unfavorable prior year reserve development and secured $1.2 billion in protection against further adverse development, causing the stock to fall 11.4% on October 28, 2025. Investors who purchased shares between February 8, 2024 and October 27, 2025 can join the lawsuit with a December 28, 2026 deadline.

items.title: Honeywell Aerospace, Inc. Notice of November 23, 2026 Application Deadline for Class Action Lawsuit - Contact Lewis Kahn, Esq. at Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC, Before Application Deadline
items.summary: Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC announced class action securities lawsuits against Honeywell Aerospace, Everest Group, and Millrose Properties for alleged securities fraud. Honeywell Aerospace is accused of failing to disclose supplier concentration risks, supply constraints, and a false Claims Act investigation related to cybersecurity compliance on government contracts. Investors who purchased shares during specified periods can seek lead plaintiff status before application deadlines.

items.title: The Ensign Group, Inc. Notice of December 7, 2026 Application Deadline for Class Action Lawsuit - Contact Lewis Kahn, Esq. at Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC, Before Application Deadline
items.summary: A class action securities lawsuit has been filed against The Ensign Group, Inc. for allegedly making materially false statements and failing to disclose systematic neglect of elderly residents in its facilities. The lawsuit covers investors who purchased Ensign securities between February 10, 2022 and June 18, 2026. Investors have until December 7, 2026 to request appointment as lead plaintiff.

items.title: Intel vs. SK Hynix: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy?
items.summary: SK Hynix is recommended as the better investment choice over Intel for the near term. SK Hynix benefits from surging AI memory demand with record revenue growth of 46.8% and a 44.2% net margin, while Intel faces execution risks in its foundry transition, weaker PC demand, and missed guidance expectations. SK Hynix trades at a significantly lower valuation multiple (3x forward P/E vs. Intel's 33.3x).

items.title: Amazon’s Cloud Computing Business Already Brings in More Revenue Than 476 Companies in the S&P 500. Here’s What It Would Take to Reach $1 Trillion.
items.summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has reached $161.4 billion in trailing-12-month revenue, surpassing 476 S&P 500 companies. CEO Andy Jassy believes AWS could become a $1 trillion revenue business within 5-10 years. With accelerating revenue growth exceeding 40% expected in 2027-2028 and substantial capital expenditure investments in AI infrastructure, AWS appears positioned to achieve this ambitious target through sustained cloud adoption and improved returns on invested capital.

items.title: ALPHABET (GOOG) ALERT: Bragar Eagel & Squire, P.C Urgently Reminds Alphabet Inc. Investors to Contact the Firm Seeking Lead Plaintiff Role Before December 1st
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Alphabet Inc. on behalf of investors who purchased securities between May 19, 2026 and July 16, 2026. The complaint alleges that Alphabet made materially false and misleading statements by failing to disclose that the Gemini 3.5 Pro was delivering disappointing training results and would face significant launch delays. Investors have until December 1, 2026 to apply to be appointed as lead plaintiff.

items.title: INVESTOR ALERT: Pomerantz Law Firm Reminds Investors with Losses on their Investment in Alphabet Inc. of Class Action Lawsuit and Upcoming Deadlines – GOOG
items.summary: Pomerantz Law Firm has filed a class action lawsuit against Alphabet Inc., alleging securities fraud related to misleading statements about the Gemini 3.5 Pro AI model launch. The company announced a June 2026 launch at its May I/O conference, but Bloomberg reported in July that Google was months behind schedule. The stock fell 4.4% on the news. Investors have until December 1, 2026, to join the class action.

items.title: CoreWeave Delivers Another Blowout Quarter. Is It Enough To Save the AI Trade?
items.summary: CoreWeave reported strong Q3 results with 168% revenue growth to $3.66B and improved operating margins, but concerns persist about its balance sheet. The company carries $47B in debt with interest expenses jumping to $846M per quarter and a free cash flow loss of $7.7B. While management pledged to avoid unsecured debt and expects $9B in customer prepayments in Q4, investors remain cautious given rising interest rates and the company's current ratio below 0.5.

items.title: NOVAGOLD Announces Expected Completion Date for Donlin Gold Acquisition, NYSE Listing and TSX Delisting
items.summary: NOVAGOLD has obtained shareholder approval to acquire Paulson's 40% stake in Donlin Gold, consolidating 100% ownership of the Tier One gold project in Alaska. The transaction is expected to close on December 1, 2026, with a new U.S. parent company, NovaGold Corporation, listing on NYSE under ticker 'NG' on December 2. NOVAGOLD shares will delist from NYSE American and TSX following completion.

items.title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 10: Trade Desk Jumps After Q3 Results Show Revenue Topped Estimates
items.summary: The Trade Desk (TTD) surged 3.28% to $15.42 after Q3 results beat revenue estimates at $736 million. The company announced a $731 million buyback authorization increase, bringing total repurchase capacity to $1 billion. While Q4 guidance won't show year-over-year growth, management signaled confidence in the turnaround. Trading volume reached 64.9 million shares, 189% above average. The broader market declined with S&P 500 down 0.38% and Nasdaq down 0.74%.
