items.summary: Earnings Flash (FRU.TO) Freehold Royalties Ltd. Reports Q3 Revenue CA$100.3M    marketscreener.com

items.title: Kimbell Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Oil Upside and Drilling Growth
items.summary: Kimbell Royalty Partners (KRP) missed Q3 earnings and revenue estimates but maintained Q4 guidance, reporting record production of 27,565 Boe/d (up 7%) and 93 active rigs. The company expects stronger Q4 cash flow with 84% of oil production unhedged, completed $367M in acquisitions, and announced a $0.45 per unit distribution representing 75% of cash available for distribution.

items.title: ROSEN, THE FIRST FILING FIRM, Encourages The Ensign Group, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action First Filed by the Firm - ENSG
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is urging investors who purchased securities of The Ensign Group, Inc. (ENSG) between February 10, 2022 and June 18, 2026 to secure legal counsel before the December 7, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline. The lawsuit alleges that Ensign made false statements regarding its business model, claiming the company systematically neglected elderly residents, defrauded Medicare and Medicaid, falsified nursing assistant hours, and engaged in illegal licensing schemes while understating litigation risks.

items.title: 3 AI Stocks to Buy Now That Midterms Are Over
items.summary: Following the midterm elections, concerns about the AI trade have eased, particularly in Texas where data center construction pipelines remain safe through 2027-2028. Three AI stocks are positioned to benefit: Penguin Solutions, which specializes in memory products for data centers with 68% YoY revenue growth; Sandisk, whose NAND flash memory chips are essential for AI infrastructure with 378% YoY revenue growth; and Alphabet, which is advancing AI through Gemini and Waymo while Google Cloud revenue more than doubled YoY.

items.title: Devon Energy Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Permian Focus and Buybacks
items.summary: Devon Energy reported Q3 adjusted earnings of $1.42 per share, beating consensus estimates of $1.24, though revenues missed expectations. The company outlined a 2027 capital spending plan of $5.3B with 75% directed to Permian Basin development, increased merger synergies to $700M, and accelerated shareholder returns including over $1B in Q4 buybacks and $1.5B in debt reduction.

items.title: Top Stock Picks for Week of November 9, 2026
items.summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) strengthens its semiconductor market position through strong AI infrastructure demand for EPYC server CPUs and Instinct accelerators, with earnings expected to grow 90.9% in the current quarter and 92.8% for the fiscal year. Moderna raises its 2026 revenue outlook following stronger-than-expected Q3 sales, with third-quarter revenues increasing 29% year-over-year, supported by increased COVID vaccine demand and international partnerships.

items.title: Reasons to Hold Veeva Systems Stock in Your Portfolio for Now
items.summary: Veeva Systems (VEEV) is well-positioned for growth driven by its diversified product portfolio, strong Q2 fiscal 2027 results, and accelerating Vault CRM adoption with over 180 customers live and 12 of top 20 biopharma commitments. However, market saturation in the life sciences CRM sector poses a headwind to future growth rates. The company raised its fiscal 2027 outlook and expects 35% growth over the next five years.

items.title: Can Home Depot Sustain Comparable Sales Growth Amid Uneven Demand?
items.summary: Home Depot reported Q2'26 comparable sales growth of 1.7% year-over-year, driven by professional customer demand and 11% digital sales growth across 13 of 16 departments. However, comparable transactions declined 1%, indicating ticket-driven rather than volume-led growth. The company reaffirmed flat to 2% comps guidance for FY26 as persistent housing affordability pressures and consumer uncertainty continue to constrain larger discretionary renovation projects.

items.title: ROSEN, GLOBAL INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Duolingo, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - DUOL
items.summary: A securities class action lawsuit has been filed against Duolingo, Inc. alleging that the company made materially false statements regarding Daily Active User growth rates. The lawsuit claims Duolingo deliberately added user friction through increased ads and subscription upsells while using AI-generated content that degraded product quality, negatively impacting user retention and financial performance. Investors who purchased Duolingo Class A common stock between May 2, 2025 and February 26, 2026 may be eligible for compensation. The lead plaintiff deadline is December 7, 2026.

items.title: EFX Stock Rallies 13% in 6 Months: Here's What You Should Know
items.summary: Equifax (EFX) gained 12.9% over six months, outperforming industry expectations through diversified revenue growth across Workforce Solutions, U.S. Information Solutions, and International operations. The company doubled its AI-driven cost-savings target to $150M and raised 2026 margin expansion guidance to 100 bps. Government contract wins exceeding $550M annually support continued Workforce Solutions growth, with the company successfully navigating weak mortgage market conditions.

items.title: Franklin Templeton Lifts 2029 Targets: What's Driving Its Optimism?
items.summary: Franklin Templeton (BEN) raised its fiscal 2029 adjusted operating margin target to 35% from 30%, driven by aggressive expansion in private markets (targeting $150B fundraising), ETFs (targeting $200B AUM), and customized investment solutions. The company has already raised $66B in private markets since fiscal 2024 and achieved 73% year-over-year ETF AUM growth to $84.6B in fiscal 2026. Despite execution risks from market volatility and fee pressures, BEN's diversified capabilities position it for sustained long-term growth.

items.title: Lam Research's Gross Margin Hits 52.4%: Can it Climb Further?
items.summary: Lam Research achieved a record non-GAAP gross margin of 52.4% in Q1'27, driven by strong revenue growth of 22%, favorable customer mix, and 40% year-over-year growth in its Customer Support Business Group. The company expects a 52.5% gross margin in Q2, though customer-mix headwinds and supply constraints may limit further gains. Competitors Applied Materials and KLA also showed strong margin expansion, benefiting from AI-driven semiconductor equipment demand.

items.title: Kimberly-Clark Has Raised Its Dividend for 55 Straight Years. Here's How Much $10,000 Invested Pays Annually.
items.summary: Kimberly-Clark, a Dividend King with 55 consecutive years of dividend increases, offers investors a $10,000 stake generating approximately $471 annually in dividends with growth potential. The company recently completed its $49 billion acquisition of Kenvue, adding major brands like Listerine and Tylenol while targeting $1.9 billion in cost efficiencies over three years. Consumer staples stocks like KMB are gaining favor as alternatives to the vulnerable AI trade.

items.title: Can Comfort Systems' Mechanical Margins Offset Electrical Weakness?
items.summary: Comfort Systems USA (FIX) delivered strong Q3 2026 results with Mechanical revenues up 43% and Electrical revenues surging 85%. While Mechanical segment margins expanded 80 basis points to 25.1%, Electrical margins declined 190 basis points to 24.3%, primarily due to absence of prior-year discrete gains. Consolidated operating margin improved to 16.6%, and the company expects 2027 gross margins to remain strong. FIX stock has outperformed its industry and the S&P 500 YTD, trading at a forward P/E of 17.7 with upward earnings revisions.

items.title: VST Q3 Earnings Beat on Strong Power Pricing, Revenues Rise Y/Y
items.summary: Vistra Corp. reported Q3 2026 earnings of $3.23 per share, beating estimates by 9.86% with an 84.6% year-over-year increase. Revenues reached $6.35 billion, up 27.7% but slightly missing consensus estimates. The company raised 2026 guidance and initiated 2027 outlook, supported by higher energy prices, the Cogentrix acquisition, and strong retail performance. Peer utilities Everergy, FirstEnergy, and IDACORP also reported better-than-expected Q3 results.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges AppLovin Corporation Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against AppLovin Corporation alleging securities fraud. The complaint claims that between February 12, 2026 and August 5, 2026, AppLovin made false and misleading statements regarding its generative AI video creative feature, overstating AI model improvements and the benefits of its 'virtuous cycle' value proposition. Investors who purchased AppLovin securities during this period are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of November 16, 2026.

items.title: Embraer Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates, Revenues Beat, Outlook Raised
items.summary: Embraer (EMBJ) missed Q3 earnings expectations with 40 cents per ADS versus consensus of 87 cents, though revenues grew 17.2% to $2.35 billion. The company delivered 66 aircraft and achieved a record $35.7 billion backlog. EMBJ raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $8.4-$8.6 billion and increased free cash flow outlook to at least $700 million, earning a Zacks Rank #1 Strong Buy rating.

items.title: GEHC Expands Vscan Air AI Capabilities With Lung Guidance & AutoAS
items.summary: GE HealthCare Technologies announced the addition of two AI-assisted features—Lung Guidance and AutoAS—to its Vscan Air handheld ultrasound system. Lung Guidance achieved a 95.2% success rate for diagnostic-quality lung exams among non-expert users, while AutoAS aids in aortic stenosis assessment. These additions expand GE HealthCare's point-of-care ultrasound capabilities and could drive adoption and recurring revenue through Innovation Packages.

items.title: Is Now the Right Time to Hold Labcorp Stock in Your Portfolio?
items.summary: Labcorp Holdings (LH) has surged 48.2% year-to-date, driven by expansion in specialty testing markets, AI and automation initiatives, and six consecutive quarters of margin expansion. However, currency headwinds, intense competition, and acquisition-related execution risks could limit future growth. The company maintains a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) with a 5% earnings yield.

items.title: Watsco: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Watsco reported 7% sales growth to $2.22 billion in Q3 2026, driven by HVAC volume and pricing gains. The company is expanding into plumbing distribution, leveraging its debt-free balance sheet and proprietary software to increase contractor loyalty and market share. Management targets a 30% gross margin through operational efficiency and views strategic M&A as key to compounding market share over the next three to five years.

items.title: McDonald's vs Wendy's: What's the Better Fast-Food Stock to Buy Right Now?
items.summary: McDonald's and Wendy's represent two different investment approaches in fast food. McDonald's offers stability with steady 1.5% comparable sales growth, a 50-year dividend increase streak, and a 2.64% yield, making it ideal for risk-averse investors. Wendy's, down 60% over five years with declining same-store sales, is pursuing a turnaround strategy called 'Dave's Way' and trades at a lower valuation with a 5.90% yield, offering potential upside for high-risk investors despite recent dividend cuts.

items.title: SHAREHOLDER ALERT: Bronstein Gewirtz & Grossman, LLC Announces Class Action Against Lululemon Athletica Inc. (NASDAQ: LULU) — Investors Who Suffered Losses Are Encouraged to Contact the Firm
items.summary: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman, LLC has filed class action lawsuits against Lululemon Athletica, Chemours Company, and O-I Glass for alleged securities fraud. Lululemon is accused of failing to disclose deteriorating store traffic and demand due to negative media commentary and weak product launches, while misrepresenting its financial guidance and turnaround plans. Investors in these companies during specified periods are encouraged to seek recovery.

items.title: TTD Q3 Earnings Call Focuses on Resetting Growth and Execution
items.summary: The Trade Desk reported Q3 2026 revenues of $736 million, down 0.5% year-over-year but beating consensus estimates. Despite the beat, management emphasized the turnaround remains incomplete. The company projects cautious Q4 guidance of at least $755 million in revenue with no expected seasonal uplift. TTD is implementing a 15% workforce reduction generating $44M in restructuring charges, targeting over $100M in gross savings for 2027 while investing in AI, measurement, and customer relationships. International growth remains strong, but large global advertisers face continued pressure.

items.title: MonetizeMore Launches AdSense Policy Grader to Help Publishers Prevent Google Ad Bans
items.summary: MonetizeMore announced the AdSense Policy Grader (APG), an AI-powered audit tool that checks publisher websites against Google's policies. The tool offers a free 40-point check report and a paid $19.99 comprehensive 79-check report, helping publishers identify and fix compliance issues before they result in revenue loss or account termination. According to Google's 2025 report, over 480 million publisher pages had ads blocked or restricted in 2025.

items.title: TTWO Q2 Earnings Call Highlights GTA VI Outlook and Booking Trends
items.summary: Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) reported Q2 fiscal 2027 earnings of $1.00 per share, beating estimates by 11.10%, but revenues of $1.60 billion missed forecasts by 3.40% with an 18.32% year-over-year decline. The company maintained its $8-$8.2B fiscal 2027 bookings guidance, supported by strong Grand Theft Auto VI preorders ahead of its November 19 launch. NBA 2K27 underperformed expectations despite 4 million units sold, while mobile titles showed mixed results. Management emphasized cost discipline and cash flow focus.

items.title: QMCO Q2 Earnings Call Centers on Tape Demand and Supply Limits
items.summary: Quantum Corporation (QMCO) reported hyperscale tape demand surged 2.6x year-over-year with a record ~$100M backlog, driven by AI-related data growth and infrastructure cost control needs. However, component availability remains a bottleneck limiting revenue upside. Q3 guidance of $91M (+22% YoY) depends on tape drive supply recovery, with IBM doubling production and Fujifilm expanding capacity. The company maintains a 43% gross margin target over 18 months while managing divergent customer trends across mid-market, enterprise, and hyperscale segments.

items.title: ZETA Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Growth and Higher Outlook
items.summary: Zeta Global reported Q3 2026 revenues of $492.7 million, up 46% year-over-year, with adjusted EPS of 38 cents beating consensus estimates. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $1.853-$1.857 billion (42% growth) driven by accelerating Athena AI platform adoption, which now represents over 70% of revenues. Management highlighted expanding enterprise opportunities through AthenaOS and strategic partnerships with Palantir and OpenAI, while improving profitability with adjusted EBITDA up 55% and free cash flow up 73%.

items.title: AMD vs. Intel: Which Is the Better Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chip Stock to Buy Right Now?
items.summary: AMD is outpacing Intel in the AI chip market with 97% year-over-year data center revenue growth compared to Intel's 78%. AMD expects data center revenue to more than double in 2027 with 80%+ overall revenue growth, significantly outpacing Intel's 13% guidance. Despite trading at similar valuations, AMD's projected 118% EPS growth in 2027 versus Intel's 20% makes it the better investment choice.

items.title: CME vs. PayPal: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
items.summary: The article compares CME Group and PayPal as investment options for 2027. CME Group operates the leading derivatives marketplace with a strong 62% net margin and 6.4% revenue growth, while PayPal operates a massive 439-million-account network with a lower 15.8% net margin but trades at a significantly cheaper valuation (P/E of 11.45 vs. 24.97). Despite PayPal's attractive valuation, the author recommends CME Group for its superior revenue growth, higher profitability margins, and stronger historical performance over the past decade.

items.title: Is CNH Industrials Stock Worth Buying After Q3 2026 Results?
items.summary: CNH Industrial is strengthening its agricultural equipment business through precision technology investments and a planned construction equipment joint venture with Kobelco, which should generate ~$700 million in cash for debt reduction. However, weak regional demand (particularly in South America), tariff pressures, rising credit risks, and working capital challenges continue to constrain financial performance, leading to a neutral investment outlook.

items.title: CME vs. S&P Global: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
items.summary: The article compares CME Group and S&P Global as investment options for 2027. CME operates the world's leading derivatives marketplace with an impressive 62% net margin and pays a higher dividend yield of 1.68%. S&P Global provides critical credit ratings and financial data with more diversified revenue streams and higher absolute revenue ($15.3B vs $6.5B). Despite CME's superior profitability metrics, the author recommends S&P Global because CME has underperformed the S&P 500 by over 100 percentage points over the past decade, suggesting the trend may not reverse.

items.title: Time to Buy Nvidia-Heavy ETFs as CEO Huang's Affair Turns Into a Spy Plot?
items.summary: NVIDIA shares fell 4.3% ($193 billion in market value) following CEO Jensen Huang's admission of an extramarital affair and a board investigation into potential foreign espionage. While NVIDIA's AI fundamentals remain strong with 106% revenue growth, succession uncertainty and key-man risk pose near-term concerns. The article recommends NVIDIA-heavy ETFs as a diversified alternative to direct stock ownership to mitigate single-stock volatility.

items.title: Can ConocoPhillips Sustain Future Production Growth With Lower CapEx?
items.summary: ConocoPhillips plans to achieve low-single-digit production growth in 2027 while reducing capital spending, leveraging operational efficiencies in its Permian Basin assets and recently commissioned Canadian operations. The company targets a $7 billion free cash flow improvement by 2029 through cost reductions and efficiency gains, despite inflationary pressures on fuel, logistics, and chemicals.

items.title: Sandisk Stock Has Collapsed by 65%, but It's Still Undergoing an 8-for-1 Stock Split on Nov. 19. Here's Why I'm Still Not Buying Shares Amidst This Nasdaq Market Slump.
items.summary: SanDisk stock has plummeted 65% from its June peak despite strong current financials driven by AI infrastructure demand and memory chip shortages. While the stock appears cheap at a P/E of 3.5, the author warns investors to avoid buying ahead of the November 19 stock split, citing the cyclical nature of the memory chip market. The author projects that when supply normalizes and pricing power diminishes, SanDisk's earnings could collapse significantly, making the stock potentially overvalued at current levels.

items.title: BigBear.ai Expands Gross Margin by 878 Bps: What Drives the Gains?
items.summary: BigBear.ai (BBAI) reported Q3 2026 gross margin expansion of 878 basis points to 31.2% with 31% revenue growth to $43.6 million, driven by its generative AI platform adoption across federal agencies. The company raised 2026 revenue guidance to $150-$165 million and increased backlog to $330 million. However, adjusted EBITDA remains negative at $9.1 million, and the company faces intense competition from larger rivals like Palantir with significantly higher margins.

items.title: Newmont Stock Up 26% YTD: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: Newmont (NEM) shares have gained 25.8% YTD, outperforming peers and the S&P 500, driven by higher realized gold prices and operational efficiency. The company is advancing key growth projects like Cadia Panel Caves and Tanami Expansion while maintaining strong liquidity of $12.8 billion. However, declining gold production (9% YoY in Q3) and rising costs pose headwinds to profitability, despite reduced 2026 cost guidance. Zacks rates NEM as a Hold.

The company returns value to shareholders through dividends (1.6% yield) and a $3 billion share buyback program. However, investors should be aware of risks including a high P/E ratio of 31x, rising operational costs, and a substantial $23 billion net debt load that becomes more expensive with elevated interest rates.

items.title: Axon's Connected Devices Unit Gains Momentum: Can It Sustain?
items.summary: Axon Enterprise (AXON) reported strong demand for TASER 10 and Axon Body 4 cameras, with Platform Solutions revenues surging 105.6%. However, the company lowered its 2026 revenue guidance to $3.61-$3.63 billion (30% growth) from 32-34% due to delays in three federal Dedrone projects worth approximately $130 million.

items.title: Can EMCOR Keep Its 10.5% Adjusted Margin as Project Volumes Scale?
items.summary: EMCOR Group (EME) reported Q3 2026 revenues up 28.8% to $5.54 billion with adjusted EPS climbing 46% to $9.60, supported by record RPOs of $18.57 billion. The company raised 2026 guidance to $34.50-$35.50 adjusted EPS. However, Mechanical Construction margins declined 80 basis points, and the investment case hinges on converting strong demand into profitable execution. Stock has declined 34.6% over six months but trades at a premium valuation with a forward P/E of 15.34.

items.title: INTC Stock Down 57% in the Past 6 Months: Should You Exercise Caution?
items.summary: Intel shares have plummeted 56.5% over six months, significantly underperforming peers amid weak Q4 guidance projecting $15-16B in revenues and a 20%+ sequential decline in PC segment revenues. The company faces headwinds from PC market weakness, China trade restrictions, and supply chain disruptions. However, Intel's foundry business shows promise with 58% year-over-year revenue growth to $6.7B, supported by advanced manufacturing nodes and AI infrastructure investments. Despite margin pressures and near-term challenges, positive earnings estimate revisions and long-term AI opportunities suggest cautious optimism for long-term investors.

items.title: ZTS Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Competitive Pressures and Outlook
items.summary: Zoetis reported Q3 adjusted earnings of $1.75 per share, beating estimates of $1.51, with revenues of $2.39 billion exceeding expectations despite a 1% year-over-year decline. The company raised 2026 EPS guidance to $6.25-$6.35 and narrowed revenue outlook to $9.22-$9.32 billion. Companion animal demand remains pressured, but targeted promotions reduced dermatology market share losses, while livestock revenues grew 7% and diagnostics increased 13%.

items.title: DKNG Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Predictions Spending and 2027 Outlook
items.summary: DraftKings reported Q3 2026 results with 16% revenue growth to $1.33B but missed estimates and posted wider losses of 53 cents per share. The company cut 2026 EBITDA guidance due to $650-700M investment in its Predictions market platform, while projecting stronger 2027 performance with core adjusted EBITDA of $1.15-1.25B. Sportsbook revenues surged 36% year-over-year, though regulatory uncertainty around sports contracts remains a key risk.

items.title: Cloudflare Q3 Earnings Call Puts AI Demand and Margins in Focus
items.summary: Cloudflare reported Q3 2026 revenues of $782.5M, up 39% and beating estimates, driven by variable usage and enterprise expansion. The company surpassed 10M active developers, improved dollar-based net retention to 122%, and advanced its GAAP profitability target to Q4 2026. Management highlighted strong demand for developer infrastructure, security solutions, and emerging AI agent revenue models, while maintaining operating discipline with a 17.5% non-GAAP operating margin.

items.title: ASML reports transactions under its current share buyback program
items.summary: ASML Holding N.V. reported share buyback transactions conducted between November 2-6, 2026, repurchasing a total of 422,800 shares at weighted average prices ranging from €1,258.16 to €1,417.24 per share, totaling approximately €562.8 million. The buyback program was announced on January 28, 2026.

items.title: Can Altria's 64.5% Smokeable Margin Sustain Profit Growth Ahead?
items.summary: Altria Group reported Q3 2026 smokeable segment adjusted OCI of $3.07B, up 3.9% year-over-year, with margins expanding to 64.5%. Strong pricing (4.4% price realization) and tax refunds offset declining cigarette shipments (-2.9%) and higher costs. Marlboro's premium share reached 60%, while the company faces ongoing industry headwinds from reduced cigarette demand.

items.title: Buy 5 Non-Tech Nasdaq Stocks to Enhance Your Portfolio Returns in Q4
items.summary: While the Nasdaq rally has been primarily driven by AI technology stocks, five non-tech Nasdaq-listed companies with Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) ratings are positioned for growth. APA Corp benefits from cost savings and long-term projects, Casey's General Stores gains from inside sales momentum and fuel margins, eBay leverages marketplace innovation, Hasbro benefits from gaming demand, and Equinix capitalizes on AI infrastructure growth.

items.title: Recent Price Trend in Transcat (TRNS) is Your Friend, Here's Why
items.summary: Transcat, Inc. (TRNS) is highlighted as a suitable candidate for short-term trend investors based on Zacks' 'Recent Price Strength' screen. The stock has gained 8.3% over 12 weeks and 17.7% over the past four weeks, currently trading at 85.1% of its 52-week high-low range. TRNS carries a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating and an Average Broker Recommendation of #1, indicating strong fundamental strength and positive near-term price performance outlook.

items.title: TECH Q1 Earnings & Revenues Beat, Merck KGaA Merger Deal Advances
items.summary: Bio-Techne (TECH) reported Q1 FY2027 adjusted EPS of 44 cents, up 4.8% YoY and beating estimates by 10%, with revenues growing 5% to $299.7M. Protein Sciences segment revenues rose 9% to $219.7M, while Diagnostics and Spatial Biology grew modestly at 1%. Shareholders approved the merger with Merck KGaA valued at $11.3 billion ($73/share), expected to close by late 2026 or early 2027.

items.title: Diamondback Energy Sees New Revenue Potential in AI Power Boom
items.summary: Diamondback Energy (FANG) is pursuing new revenue streams by supplying natural gas and infrastructure to support AI data center power generation in West Texas. The company's Bryant Ranch power project is nearing completion pending final commercial agreements, while its 7.5% stake in the Solitude Pipeline System aims to improve access to LNG and downstream markets. With strong Q3 2026 cash flow of $2.15 billion and projected 2026 free cash flow of $9.2 billion, FANG has financial capacity to pursue these opportunities alongside its core oil and gas operations.

items.title: Could Kraft Heinz's Latest Move Be a Sign That a Dividend Cut Is Around the Corner?
items.summary: Kraft Heinz is selling its North American coffee business to One Rock Capital Partners for $500 million in net proceeds to pay down debt. The move signals financial strain, as the company's earnings have declined and its dividend payout ratio is high relative to earnings. With diluted per-share profit of $0.46 last quarter versus a quarterly dividend of $0.40, there is minimal buffer, raising concerns about the sustainability of the dividend and the possibility of a future dividend cut.

items.title: MRK's 2027 Outlook Challenging, Long-Term Prospects Promising
items.summary: Merck reported strong Q3 2026 results but expects modest 2027 revenue growth due to over $2 billion in generic drug competition and vaccine business challenges. Keytruda faces biosimilar competition around 2028-2029, potentially causing sharp sales declines. However, the company projects over $70 billion in potential pipeline opportunities by the mid-2030s to drive future growth.

items.title: Cummins After Q3: Is the Stock a Buy on AI Data Center Boom?
items.summary: Cummins Inc. reported Q3 2026 revenues of $9.44B (up 13.5% YoY) but missed earnings estimates due to supply constraints and weak truck demand. The company's Power Systems segment showed strong growth (15% sales increase) driven by AI data center demand, with orders extending into 2028. However, North American pickup engine shipments fell 16% YoY, prompting full-year guidance cuts. While the long-term AI infrastructure opportunity is compelling, supply bottlenecks and truck market weakness support a hold rating rather than a buy.

items.title: Nebius Stock Ahead of Q3 Earnings: Should You Buy, Hold or Sell?
items.summary: Nebius Group (NBIS) is expected to beat Q3 2026 earnings estimates with an Earnings ESP of +50.82% and revenue estimate of $916.78M, driven by strong AI cloud infrastructure demand, rising GPU prices, and capacity expansion. However, the company faces headwinds from substantial capital expenditure requirements ($20-25B annually) and infrastructure deployment timing challenges. NBIS shares trade at a lower P/B ratio (3.17X) compared to the industry average (3.49X).

items.title: Arm and Qualcomm Lead Mobile Chip Design. 1 Stock Is the Better Buy.
items.summary: Qualcomm and Arm Holdings, leaders in mobile chip design, both saw their stock prices plummet 14% following earnings reports on November 4. Qualcomm missed earnings estimates while Arm provided a weaker-than-expected outlook. Despite Arm's superior market position and growth prospects, its valuation at 220x P/E is too expensive. Qualcomm trades cheaper at 19x earnings but faces margin pressures. The author recommends waiting for better valuations before buying either stock.

items.title: Amazon’s Cloud Business Just Did Something It Hasn’t Done in Nearly Five Years
items.summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) achieved its fastest revenue growth in nearly five years at 39% year-over-year, reaching $46 billion in Q3 2026, with operating income up 55%. The unit now has a $578 billion contracted revenue backlog and a $184 billion annual revenue run rate. However, Amazon's massive $220 billion capital spending forecast continues to weigh on free cash flow, raising investor concerns about whether AI demand will justify the enormous infrastructure investments.

items.title: Cinemark and Whirlpool have been highlighted as Zacks Bull and Bear of the Day
items.summary: Zacks Equity Research designated Cinemark Holdings as the Bull of the Day following record Q3 results with 23.5% YoY revenue growth and 160% earnings growth, driven by strong film slate and premium experiences. Whirlpool was named the Bear of the Day due to weak appliance demand, falling sales, and a significant downward earnings guidance revision from $2.50-$3.00 to -$1.30 per share. The article also analyzes NVIDIA and AMD, concluding NVIDIA is the better buy-the-dip opportunity given superior profitability metrics.

items.title: ROSEN, A LONGSTANDING FIRM, Encourages Everest Group, Ltd. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - EG
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is notifying investors about multiple ongoing securities class action lawsuits. The primary case involves Everest Group, Ltd., where investors who purchased stock between February 8, 2024 and October 27, 2025 may be entitled to compensation. The lawsuit alleges Everest made false statements about casualty risk exposure, inadequate pricing, and insufficient reserves. Additional class actions are mentioned for Lincoln Educational Services Corporation and Dun & Bradstreet Holdings, Inc., with a November 10, 2026 deadline.

items.title: Lululemon Athletica vs. On: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
items.summary: The article compares Lululemon Athletica and On as investment options for 2027. Lululemon offers steady profits with $11.1B revenue but faces declining sales (-4% in Q2 2026), legal challenges, and CEO transition. On demonstrates impressive 13.5% revenue growth with $3.7B revenue and operates in an earlier growth stage with fewer stores. The author recommends On due to its higher growth trajectory and earlier stage of expansion, despite its premium valuation multiple.

items.title: Procter & Gamble's Dividend Has Survived 26 Recessions. Here's What $10,000 Now Earns in Yearly Dividend Income.
items.summary: Procter & Gamble maintains its status as a Dividend King with 70 consecutive years of dividend increases, surviving 26 recessions since 1890. A $10,000 investment yields approximately $265-$269 annually at the current 2.6% yield. Despite facing $1.4 billion in higher commodity and energy costs, P&G showed resilience with 4% organic sales growth across all product categories and regions. The company's conservative payout ratio of two-thirds earnings and essential consumer staples business position it well for future recessions.

items.title: This Stock Is a Nearly Guaranteed Winner From the AI Infrastructure Buildout
items.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) is positioned as an attractive AI infrastructure investment, controlling 72.5% of global foundry revenue with no viable competitors. The company supplies chips to major AI manufacturers like Nvidia and AMD, with projected AI chip revenue growth of mid-to-high 50% annually through 2029. Trading at 23x forward earnings—a discount to historical levels—TSMC offers both long-term AI exposure and near-term value.

items.title: SHAREHOLDER ALERT: Bronstein Gewirtz & Grossman, LLC Announces Class Action Against Bank of America Corporation (NYSE: BAC) — Investors Who Suffered Losses Are Encouraged to Contact the Firm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Bank of America Corporation alleging the bank made false and misleading statements regarding its Bank Secrecy Act and Anti-Money Laundering compliance program. The complaint claims BAC failed to properly monitor trillions in transactions, missed or delayed suspicious activity reports, and had unresolved compliance deficiencies despite a 2024 Consent Order. Investors who purchased BAC securities between August 1, 2025 and October 13, 2026 may be eligible to recover losses, with a lead plaintiff deadline of December 15, 2026.

items.title: Not Bloom Energy. Not Vistra. This AI Power Stock Just Posted a 96% Jump in Orders.
items.summary: GE Vernova reported a 96% year-over-year increase in orders for power-generating equipment, with a $197 billion backlog (over 4 years of revenue). Despite a post-election sell-off in power stocks, the company's business remains resilient as 80% of customers are traditional utility companies unaffected by AI industry fluctuations.

items.title: SHAREHOLDER ALERT: Bronstein Gewirtz & Grossman, LLC Announces Class Action Against Honeywell Aerospace, Inc. (NASDAQ: HONA) — Investors Who Suffered Losses Are Encouraged to Contact the Firm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA) alleging that the company made materially false statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts during the period of June 29, 2026 to September 1, 2026. The complaint alleges undisclosed supplier concentration risks, supply constraints, a false Claims Act investigation related to cybersecurity compliance on government contracts, and that positive statements about the company lacked reasonable basis. Investors who suffered losses may be eligible to recover damages, with a lead plaintiff deadline of November 23, 2026.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges AST SpaceMobile, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against AST SpaceMobile, Inc. alleging securities fraud for the period between March 4, 2025 and July 15, 2026. The complaint claims defendants made false statements regarding the company's capital requirements, liquidity position, competitive standing in the satellite direct-to-cell market, and user adoption rates in the US and Japan. Investors who purchased ASTS securities during this period are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of November 13, 2026.

items.title: Why Royalty Pharma Investors Could Be the Quiet Winners From Revolution Medicines' Groundbreaking Pancreatic Cancer Drug
items.summary: Revolution Medicines' pancreatic cancer drug daraxonrasib received FDA approval and could generate peak revenues of $11 billion. Royalty Pharma, which financed the drug, stands to earn up to $340 million in peak royalties without doing the development work. While Revolution Medicines stock has surged 200% in the past year, Royalty Pharma offers a more diversified alternative with investments in 35 approved drugs and a 1.4% dividend yield.

items.title: AI Power Stocks Just Fell 6.3% to 9.3% on Financing Fears. SpaceX Just Said New Compute Pays Back in Under a Year.
items.summary: AI power stocks GE Vernova and Bloom Energy fell on financing concerns, but SpaceX reported that its new compute investments pay back in under a year with pricing above previous guidance. SpaceX's Super Intelligence segment generated $7.6B in Q3 revenue, and the company plans to expand compute capacity from 1.7 to 2.5-3 gigawatts by year-end, with potential for 10 additional gigawatts in 2027, though massive capex requirements present execution risks.

items.title: Prediction: This Will Be the Best-Performing AI Stock of 2027
items.summary: Micron Technology is predicted to be the best-performing AI stock of 2027, having already gained over 200% in 2026. The company benefits from strong demand for memory chips used in AI computing, with tight supply conditions expected to persist through 2027-2028. A new production facility launching mid-2027 combined with high prices could drive significant revenue and profit growth, potentially resulting in 4x-5x stock gains if the company returns to historical valuation multiples.

items.title: 3 Reasons Why Ultra High Yield Realty Income Is a Buy After Its Latest Earnings Report
items.summary: Realty Income reported solid third-quarter 2026 earnings with modest guidance increases and another annual dividend hike, demonstrating resilience despite rising interest rates. The REIT's massive portfolio, investment-grade balance sheet, and diversified funding sources position it as a reliable income investment with a 5.6% yield.

items.title: The Trade Desk Stock Has Lost About 89% Since the End of 2024. Its Nov. 9 Report Is the Next Test.
items.summary: The Trade Desk's stock has plummeted 89% since end of 2024, trading near $13 after an August forecast miss. The ad tech company guided for Q3 revenue of at least $650 million (down 12% YoY) and faces investor scrutiny as it has recently missed its own revenue forecasts. The company's Nov. 9 earnings report will be critical to determine if guidance credibility can be restored and whether revenue declines are stabilizing.

items.title: Got $5,000? 2 Growth Stocks Building the Software Backbone of Artificial Intelligence (AI).
items.summary: The article recommends Microsoft and CrowdStrike as two complementary software stocks for AI investment. Microsoft is monetizing AI through Azure cloud services and Copilot integration, with Azure revenue up 48% year-over-year and Copilot users growing significantly. CrowdStrike is positioned to protect AI agents through its Falcon cybersecurity platform, with strong revenue growth of 26% and record net new ARR of $333 million. Both companies demonstrate strong customer demand and expansion opportunities in the growing AI market.

items.title: 1 Stat That Makes Amazon Hard to Ignore Right Now
items.summary: Amazon reported strong Q3 results with 12% year-over-year sales growth, driven primarily by AWS which grew 39% YoY. AWS is experiencing exceptional demand with Fortune 500 companies increasing Amazon Bedrock spending sevenfold and token volume increasing 17-fold. CEO Andy Jassy projects AWS sales will grow 40% in both 2027 and 2028, with potential for both e-commerce and AWS to become trillion-dollar businesses within 5-10 years. Despite concerns about negative free cash flow from AI spending, the stock recovered after initial post-earnings decline.

items.title: Airbnb: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Airbnb reported Q3 2026 revenue of $4.9 billion with 19% year-over-year growth, marking its fastest revenue growth in over 3 years. The company highlighted three key drivers: hotel listings funnel first-time users to residential properties (35% conversion within a year), AI-powered customer support reduced costs per booking by 17%, and a new $12 billion share repurchase program signals strong cash generation and balance sheet confidence.

items.title: Why AT&T Stock Slumped in October
items.summary: AT&T's stock fell over 14% in October despite beating third-quarter earnings estimates, primarily due to investor concerns about SpaceX's aggressive expansion into the consumer telecom market. SpaceX acquired wireless spectrum, secured FCC approval for its Gen2 satellite constellation, and reportedly plans to establish 80,000 cell sites across the U.S., positioning itself as a potential nationwide wireless carrier that could threaten incumbent telecom providers.

items.title: המועד האחרון בתיק ASTS: רוזן, משרד עורכי דין בעל מוניטין בינלאומי, קורא למשקיעים ב- AST SpaceMobile, Inc שספגו הפסדים העולים על 100,000 דולר, לשכור ייצוג משפטי לקראת המועד החשוב ב-13 בנובמבר במסגרת תביעה ייצוגית בניירות ערך – ASTS

The lawsuit alleges the company made false statements regarding capital needs, liquidity, competitive positioning, and user adoption rates in the satellite direct-to-consumer market.

items.title: Forget Lilly and Novo: Pfizer Is Planning a Wave of Phase 3 Obesity Trials
items.summary: While Eli Lilly dominates the GLP-1 weight-loss drug market and Novo Nordisk struggles to regain ground, Pfizer is positioning itself as a surprise contender. After dropping its original GLP-1 candidate, Pfizer acquired an alternative drug in development and is now running 10 late-stage trials. The company's key differentiator is a monthly injection option, which could offer greater convenience than competitors' weekly or daily dosing. With a high dividend yield of 5.5% and an inflection point potentially closer than Wall Street believes, Pfizer may represent an overlooked opportunity for long-term dividend investors.

items.title: SoundHound AI: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: SoundHound AI announced plans to achieve sustainable profitability in H2 2027 by shifting from unpredictable upfront licensing fees to recurring hosted subscriptions through its OASYS platform. The company identified $120 million in annualized cost reductions and is replacing external AI models with proprietary in-house technology to significantly reduce computing costs. Q3 2026 revenue grew 48% year-over-year to $62.4 million, with management emphasizing financial discipline and pricing discipline going forward.

items.title: APP 9-DAY DEADLINE ALERT: AppLovin Corporation Investors with Substantial Losses Encouraged to Contact Hagens Berman, Securities Class Action Pending
items.summary: Hagens Berman is investigating AppLovin Corporation for alleged securities law violations, claiming executives made materially false statements about AI model readiness and self-service ad tool adoption. The company's stock plummeted 19.6% on August 6, 2026, after missing revenue estimates and acknowledging significant developmental delays in generative AI video tools. Investors with substantial losses are encouraged to contact the firm by the November 16, 2026 deadline.

items.title: Booking vs. DoorDash: Does Going Out or Staying In Make One Stock a Better Buy for 2027?
items.summary: The article compares Booking Holdings and DoorDash as investment options for 2027. Booking operates a global travel reservation platform with strong profitability (20.1% net margin), generates $9.1B in free cash flow, and trades at an attractive forward P/E of 16.1x. DoorDash is a rapidly growing local delivery platform (28% revenue growth) expanding into groceries and retail, but trades at a premium forward P/E of 65.0x. The author recommends Booking for long-term investors due to its superior valuation, strong financial position, and cash generation despite both companies executing well.

items.title: BANK OF AMERICA ALERT: Bragar Eagel & Squire, P.C. Reminds Investors that a Class Action Lawsuit Has Been Filed Against Bank of America and Encourages Investors to Contact the Firm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Bank of America in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York. The suit alleges that Bank of America made false and misleading statements regarding systemic weaknesses in its Bank Secrecy Act/anti-money laundering program, which caused it to miss or inaccurately report billions of dollars in suspicious transactions. The company also allegedly failed to maintain an adequate sanctions compliance program. Investors who purchased BAC stock between August 1, 2025 and October 13, 2026 may be eligible to participate, with a deadline of December 15, 2026 to apply as lead plaintiff.

items.title: $10,000 Invested in PayPal 5 Years Ago Is Worth About $2,590 Today. The Company Has Bought Back 8.6% of Its Shares Since January.
items.summary: PayPal stock has declined 74% over the past five years, significantly underperforming the S&P 500's 75% gain. Despite the poor stock performance, the company remains profitable with an 18.8% operating margin and generated $4.1 billion in free cash flow through the first nine months of 2026. Management has aggressively repurchased 8.6% of shares, suggesting they believe the stock is undervalued at a forward P/E of 9.7. However, the bear case centers on sluggish growth, with net revenue rising only 2% last quarter, making it a risky investment until growth accelerates.

items.title: George Kurtz Just Announced Incredible News for CrowdStrike Investors and the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Industry
items.summary: CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz announced the AI Kill Switch, a new product that gives enterprises full control over AI agents in their networks by allowing immediate termination and access control. The product addresses growing security risks from AI deployment and could accelerate enterprise AI adoption. However, CrowdStrike's stock is heavily overvalued at a P/S ratio of 46.6, making it suitable only for long-term investors willing to hold for 10+ years.

items.title: Is Alphabet's Core Search Business in Trouble? Looking Past the Headline Revenue Growth Provides a Clear Answer.
items.summary: Alphabet's Google Search revenue growth slowed to 12% year-over-year in Q3 from 17% in Q2, raising concerns about AI's impact on its core business. However, deeper analysis reveals strong engagement metrics with record query growth and longer, more detailed searches. The company is successfully monetizing AI features in Search and AI Mode, with user research showing comfort with ads on these surfaces. Meanwhile, Google Cloud Platform is emerging as a major growth driver, expected to surpass Search in operating income growth by 2027. Management remains optimistic on backlog and recent acquisitions (Hailo, VORAGO) but cautious on AI spending sustainability.

items.title: KMB Q3 Earnings Call Focuses on Kenvue Integration and Growth
items.summary: Kimberly-Clark (KMB) reported Q3 2026 adjusted earnings of $1.7 per share, beating estimates, though revenues declined 0.4% to $4.13B. The company completed its Kenvue acquisition and targets $1.9B in cost synergies. Management maintained its 2026 outlook despite headwinds from China disruptions, North American softness, and $250M in inflation. The company carries a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) rating.

items.title: Duke Energy Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Rising Capital Needs
items.summary: Duke Energy narrowed its 2026 earnings guidance to $6.70-$6.80 per share while reaffirming 5-7% annual earnings growth through 2030. The company is capitalizing on accelerating data center demand, targeting to convert its 15.4-GW pipeline into electric service agreements by mid-2027. Duke Energy plans significant capital expansion with $103B in committed investments plus $5-10B in potential additional investments, with monthly capital spending expected to increase from $1.5B to $2B by 2027.

items.title: Cummins Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Power Demand and Truck Weakness
items.summary: Cummins Inc. (CMI) lowered its 2026 revenue growth guidance to 10% from 10-13% due to weaker North American pickup truck demand, though it maintained its EBITDA margin forecast at approximately 18.2%. The company reported strong global data center demand with Power Systems recording $2.3 billion in quarterly revenues and a 25.4% EBITDA margin, with orders extending into late 2028. CMI expects to recover approximately $200 million in delayed shipments in Q4 and plans capacity expansion through 2028.

items.title: CAH Q1 Earnings Call Highlights Raised Outlook and Specialty Growth
items.summary: Cardinal Health (CAH) raised its fiscal 2027 EPS guidance to $12.80-$13.00 after reporting Q1 earnings of $3.26 per share, beating estimates. The company benefited from strong specialty pharmaceutical demand (18% revenue growth), generics performance, and renewed contracts covering nearly two-thirds of revenues. However, the medical segment faced headwinds with profit declining 28% due to elevated petroleum costs.

items.title: IREN Q1 Earnings Call Highlights AI Growth and Deployment Delays
items.summary: IREN Limited reported Q1 FY2027 results with AI cloud revenues of $200 million (182% sequential growth) and a $20 billion revenue backlog. However, the company pushed its $4 billion operating ARR target from December 2026 to January 2027 due to customer-requested design changes and supplier delays. Management also reduced capital expenditure plans to $15 billion for the remainder of fiscal 2027, citing financing conditions rather than weakening demand. The company carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating.

items.title: Unity Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Vector Growth and AI Expansion
items.summary: Unity Software exceeded Q3 earnings expectations with 44 cents per share and $622.09M in revenues. The company's AI-powered advertising platform Unity Vector drove significant growth with 126% year-over-year revenue increase. Unity projects Q4 strategic revenue growth of 65-67% and adjusted EBITDA of $290M-$295M with 42% margins. The company achieved its first quarterly GAAP profitability since IPO and announced Unity Spark, a browser-based creation platform developed with Google.

items.title: AAOI Q3 Earnings Call Highlights 1.6T Shift and Capacity Delays
items.summary: Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI) secured a major multiyear agreement worth $1B-$1.5B with a hyperscaler customer for 1.6T transceivers, reflecting accelerating demand for next-generation optical products. However, the company faces supply constraints from digital signal processor shortages and manufacturing delays, revising its capacity targets downward and pushing its $471M monthly revenue run-rate goal to late 2027. Q4 revenues are projected at $385M-$420M.

items.title: SPG Q3 FFO Tops Estimates on Leasing Strength, Outlook Raised
items.summary: Simon Property Group (SPG) reported Q3 FFO of $3.37 per share, beating estimates by 1.5%, with revenues rising 13.3% to $1.81 billion. The company raised its 2026 FFO guidance to $13.30-$13.40 per share and increased its quarterly dividend by 4.5%. U.S. mall occupancy reached 96.5% with retailer sales per square foot up 14.8%, reflecting strong leasing momentum and higher rents.

items.title: SOUN Q3 Loss Narrower Than Expected, Revenues Miss on Licensing Shift
items.summary: SoundHound AI (SOUN) reported Q3 2026 results with a narrower-than-expected loss but revenues missing estimates at $62.4M despite 48.5% year-over-year growth. Gross margins contracted significantly due to higher AI and cloud costs. The company raised 2026 revenue guidance to $250M-$260M and reaffirmed 2027 guidance of $350M-$400M, with plans for $120M in annualized cost reductions.

items.title: Investors Heavily Search C3.ai, Inc. (AI): Here is What You Need to Know
items.summary: C3.ai (AI) is receiving significant investor attention. The company is expected to report losses in the current quarter and fiscal year, though with improving year-over-year comparisons. Revenue is projected to decline 27.5% for the current fiscal year before recovering with 11.6% growth next year. The stock holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating and trades at a premium valuation (F grade), suggesting it may perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

items.title: AKAM Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Cloud Deals and 2027 Outlook
items.summary: Akamai Technologies signed an $11.6 billion seven-year agreement with Anthropic, bringing total 2026 cloud infrastructure commitments to $14 billion. The company projects CIS revenues of $1.1-$1.3 billion in 2027 and total revenues exceeding $7 billion in 2028, with expected 75% EBITDA margins on major cloud deals. However, near-term challenges include $30 million in delayed Q4 revenues and heavy capital expenditures of $2.4-$2.6 billion in Q4, which may pressure early 2027 margins.

items.title: Salesforce Stock: The 1 Number Investors Still Need to See
items.summary: Salesforce is expanding its Agent Fabric to help enterprises monitor and manage AI agents across multiple platforms, with over 1.2 billion daily requests. While the potential for additional revenue is substantial given its large customer base, the key uncertainty remains around paid adoption rates, which have not yet been quantified.

items.title: ConocoPhillips Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Higher Commodity Prices
items.summary: ConocoPhillips (COP) reported Q3 2026 adjusted earnings of $3.27 per share, up 103.1% year-over-year and beating consensus estimates by 6.9%. The strong results were driven by a 32% increase in average realized prices to $61.40 per Boe, which offset a 4% decline in production volumes. The company generated $4.04 billion in free cash flow and returned $3.4 billion to shareholders, while increasing its quarterly dividend by 11%.

items.title: Stock-Split Watch: Is Meta Platforms Next?
items.summary: Meta Platforms announced a 2-for-1 stock split via new Class C nonvoting shares effective January 19, 2027. The split allows Meta to expand its stock pool for compensation without diluting CEO Mark Zuckerberg's voting control. While stock splits don't create inherent value, Meta's strong financials, AI-funded capital expenditures, and viral Muse consumer AI app position it as a compelling long-term AI investment.

items.title: Devon Energy (DVN) Q3 Earnings: Taking a Look at Key Metrics Versus Estimates
items.summary: Devon Energy reported Q3 2026 revenue of $6.86 billion, up 58.4% year-over-year, but missed consensus estimates by 6.39%. EPS of $1.42 beat estimates by 14.52%. The company exceeded expectations on realized prices for oil, gas, and NGLs, but fell short on production volumes and marketing revenues. Stock has underperformed the S&P 500 over the past month, though it maintains a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

items.title: ROSEN, NATIONAL INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Everest Group, Ltd. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - EG
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has filed a class action lawsuit against Everest Group, Ltd. (NYSE: EG) on behalf of investors who purchased common stock between February 8, 2024 and October 27, 2025. The lawsuit alleges that Everest made materially false and misleading statements regarding its exposure to casualty risks, inadequate pricing, insufficient reserves, and overstated earnings. Investors who wish to serve as lead plaintiff must file by December 28, 2026.

items.title: Abacus Global Management, Inc. (ABX) Surpasses Q3 Earnings Estimates
items.summary: Abacus Global Management reported Q3 2026 earnings of $0.29 per share, beating consensus estimates of $0.28, with a 3.57% earnings surprise. However, revenues of $76.88 million slightly missed expectations. The stock has gained 5.9% year-to-date, underperforming the S&P 500's 12.3% gain. Despite favorable estimate revisions earning a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), the company's industry (Financial - Miscellaneous Services) ranks in the bottom 37% of sectors.

items.title: INVESTOR ALERT: RGRD Law Announces that Webull Corporation (BULL) Investors with Substantial Losses May Seek to Lead Class Action Lawsuit Before December 7, 2026 Deadline
items.summary: Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd LLP announces a class action lawsuit against Webull Corporation, alleging the company made false statements about its independence from China. The lawsuit claims Webull misrepresented its operations as primarily U.S.-based when in fact 62% of its workforce and core operations are tied to the People's Republic of China. A House Select Committee investigation corroborated these findings, leading to a 19% stock price decline. Investors with substantial losses can seek lead plaintiff status before December 7, 2026.
