items.title: Apple, Alphabet, and Meta: 3 Big Takeaways from Recent Earnings
items.summary: Apple, Alphabet, and Meta delivered strong Q3 earnings results with robust revenue growth. Apple reached record fiscal Q4 revenue of $114.5 billion with 12% YoY growth, while Alphabet saw explosive Google Cloud growth at 103% YoY. Meta's advertising business climbed 26% YoY to $64.6 billion. AI remains a key growth driver across all three companies, though Meta flagged significant capital expenditure forecasts for 2026.

items.title: Kirby McInerney LLP Alerts Investors Who Acquired The Ensign Group, Inc. ENSG Securities Between February 10, 2022 and June 18, 2026 of Pending Lawsuit
items.summary: A federal securities class action lawsuit has been filed against The Ensign Group, Inc. for allegedly failing to disclose systematic neglect of elderly residents, abuse, Medicaid/Medicare fraud, falsification of nursing assistant hours, and illegal administrator licensing schemes. Following damaging reports from Hunterbrook Media and Muddy Waters Research in June 2026, Ensign's stock price declined significantly. The deadline to seek lead plaintiff status is December 7, 2026.

items.title: Kirby McInerney LLP Alerts Investors Who Acquired Duolingo, Inc. DUOL Securities Between May 2, 2025 and February 26, 2026 of Pending Lawsuit
items.summary: A federal securities class action lawsuit has been filed against Duolingo, Inc. for allegedly failing to disclose that increased user friction from ads and monetization efforts, combined with lower-quality AI-generated content, were negatively impacting Daily Active User growth rates. The company's stock declined significantly following three disclosure events: a 25.5% drop on November 6, 2025 after reporting slowing DAU growth and announcing a strategy shift, an 8.5% decline on January 12, 2026 following the CFO's resignation, and a 14% drop on February 27, 2026 after confirming material negative impacts on 2026 financial guidance.

items.title: D-WAVE CLASS ACTION ALERT: Bragar Eagel & Squire, P.C. Announces that a Class Action Lawsuit Has Been Filed Against D-Wave Quantum Inc. and Encourages Investors to Contact the Firm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against D-Wave Quantum Inc. (NASDAQ: QBTS) alleging that the company and its executives violated federal securities laws by making false and misleading statements about the company's business and financial prospects during the period between February 26, 2026 and August 25, 2026. Investors who purchased D-Wave securities during this period and suffered losses are encouraged to contact the law firm, with a December 14, 2026 deadline to apply as lead plaintiff.

items.title: 2 Defensive Healthcare Stocks Hitting New 52-Week Highs: ABBV & LLY
items.summary: AbbVie and Eli Lilly have reached fresh 52-week highs following strong Q3 results, offering defensive healthcare alternatives as technology stocks face valuation concerns. AbbVie benefits from robust immunology drug sales and a 5.2% dividend increase, while Eli Lilly's obesity drug franchise (Mounjaro and Zepbound) drives exceptional 39% revenue growth and raised full-year guidance.

items.title: Here's What Key Metrics Tell Us About Microchip Tech (MCHP) Q2 Earnings
items.summary: Microchip Technology reported Q2 2026 revenue of $1.62 billion, up 42.2% year-over-year, beating consensus estimates by 0.83%. EPS of $0.97 exceeded expectations by 3.19%. Key product segments showed mixed results: Mixed-signal Microcontrollers missed estimates but grew 32.5% YoY, while Analog and Other segments beat expectations with 42.8% and 65.6% YoY growth respectively. The stock holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

items.title: CoreWeave vs. Nebius: Which Is the Better AI Neocloud Stock to Own for the Next 3 Years?
items.summary: Nebius emerges as the superior AI neocloud investment over CoreWeave for a 3-year horizon. CoreWeave faces financial strain with a 0.46 current ratio and corporate bonds yielding 15% APR, requiring debt refinancing. Nebius boasts a stronger 4.03 current ratio and finances 50-60% of capex through customer prepayments. While CoreWeave currently generates more revenue ($2.6B vs $582.3M in Q2), Nebius's 454% growth rate versus CoreWeave's 112% suggests it will close the gap. Nebius's available capacity positions it better to capitalize on rising megawatt prices ($40-50M per megawatt for short-term deals), while CoreWeave's capacity is locked into long-term contracts.

items.title: Solventum (SOLV) Tops Q3 Earnings Estimates
items.summary: Solventum reported Q3 2026 earnings of $1.45 per share, beating consensus estimates of $1.35 by 7.41%, but revenues of $1.95 billion missed expectations by 1.07%. The company received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, suggesting near-term performance in line with the market. The Medical Services industry ranks in the top 45% of Zacks industries.

items.title: Devon Energy (DVN) Beats Q3 Earnings Estimates
items.summary: Devon Energy reported Q3 2026 earnings of $1.42 per share, beating consensus estimates of $1.24 and delivering a 14.52% surprise. However, revenues of $6.86 billion missed estimates by 6.39%. The stock has gained 20.5% year-to-date and holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating. HighPeak Energy is expected to report results on November 9 with projected earnings of $0.07 per share, up 133.3% year-over-year, with consensus estimates revised 340% higher in the last 30 days.

items.title: Top Stock Reports for Berkshire Hathaway, Micron & Chevron
items.summary: Zacks Research Daily features hand-picked analysis of 16 major stocks on November 5, 2026. Berkshire Hathaway receives a Neutral rating despite outperforming its industry, citing balanced risk-reward. Micron earns an Outperform rating driven by AI-led demand and strong cash generation. Chevron also receives Outperform backed by upstream portfolio growth and operational strength. Orbit International, a microcap, faces persistent losses but shows revenue visibility through expanding order books.

items.title: Advanced Micro Devices vs. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing: The AI Sell-Off Is Exposing a Critical Difference Investors Shouldn't Ignore for 2027
items.summary: Following the recent semiconductor sell-off, the article compares AMD and TSMC as AI investment opportunities for 2027. While AMD competes directly in the AI chip market with strong growth (34% revenue increase), TSMC benefits from manufacturing chips for multiple industry leaders with superior profitability (45.1% margin). TSMC is recommended as the better buy due to its lower valuation (23.8x forward P/E vs AMD's 63.0x), stronger financial position, and broader exposure to the AI industry without dependence on a single chip designer.

items.title: GPN Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Genius Growth, Margins Rise
items.summary: Global Payments reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $3.58, beating estimates by 0.3%, with adjusted net revenues rising 31% year-over-year to $3.18 billion. The company expanded operating margins by 220 basis points to 42.5% and raised its synergy target to $650 million. GPN reaffirmed full-year guidance and expects over $2 billion in shareholder returns for 2026. Peers Visa, Mastercard, and Marsh & McLennan also reported strong quarterly results.

items.title: Sempra's Q3 Earnings Outpace Estimates, Revenues Increase Y/Y
items.summary: Sempra Energy reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.40, beating estimates by 16.7% with a 26.1% year-over-year increase. The company raised its full-year 2026 GAAP EPS guidance to $7.41-$8.41 and maintained long-term EPS growth targets of 7-9%. Strong performance was driven by higher Oncor equity earnings and improved infrastructure results, though revenues slightly missed expectations.

items.title: 4 Healthcare ETFs to Tap Into Eli Lilly's Post-Q3 Earnings Rally
items.summary: Eli Lilly (LLY) jumped 10.1% following better-than-expected Q3 2026 results and raised 2026 sales guidance. The company's blockbuster drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound generated over $16 billion in combined revenues with $6 billion year-over-year growth. However, LLY trades at a premium P/E ratio of 30.91, prompting investors to consider healthcare ETFs with significant LLY weightings as a balanced alternative for exposure.

items.title: ZTS Q3 Earnings Top Estimates, 2026 Profit Outlook Improves, Stock Up
items.summary: Zoetis reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.75, beating consensus of $1.51, with total revenues of $2.4 billion slightly exceeding expectations. However, U.S. companion animal sales declined 8% due to price sensitivity and competition. The company narrowed 2026 revenue guidance while raising adjusted earnings outlook. Stock rose 7.5% on results but remains down 27.5% year-to-date.

items.title: Host Hotels' Q3 FFO Beat Estimates on Strong RevPAR Growth
items.summary: Host Hotels & Resorts (HST) beat Q3 FFO estimates with 11.4% year-over-year growth to 39 cents per share, driven by strong transient demand and higher room rates. The company raised its 2026 adjusted FFO guidance to $2.21 per share and RevPAR growth outlook to 6.75%, citing resilient leisure demand and improving business travel. HST also expanded its portfolio with acquisitions of luxury properties in New York and Dallas.

items.title: TRMB Q3 Earnings Meet Estimates as AECO Growth Lifts Revenues
items.summary: Trimble (TRMB) reported Q3 2026 non-GAAP earnings of 86 cents per share, matching consensus estimates, with revenues of $966.8 million up 7.3% year-over-year. The company's AECO segment showed strong momentum with 9% organic revenue growth and record ARR of $1.636 billion, prompting management to raise full-year AECO operating margin guidance to 36%. However, Field Systems faced recurring revenue pressure with slower ARR growth, and Transportation & Logistics growth moderated amid freight weakness. Trimble lowered full-year organic ARR growth guidance to 10% from 12-14% but slightly raised earnings outlook.

items.title: Is GNRC Worth Buying as Data Center Growth Tests Margins and Risk?
items.summary: Generac Holdings (GNRC) benefits from a $4.5B data center backlog and recovering residential demand, with potential C&I revenue doubling in 2027. However, the company faces margin compression as data center sales (lower profitability) grow faster than residential, with Q4 gross margins expected to fall to 37-38%. Valuation is attractive on forward earnings (14.6X) but less compelling on EV/EBITDA and price-to-cash-flow metrics. Production ramp execution and supply constraints remain key risks.

items.title: Eversource Energy Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates, Revenues Decline Y/Y
items.summary: Eversource Energy missed Q3 earnings expectations with non-GAAP EPS of 92 cents versus consensus of 97 cents, driven by weaker electric and gas distribution results, higher interest expenses, and regulatory challenges. Despite the miss, the company raised 2026 EPS guidance to $4.62-$4.70 and maintained its $26.5B capital investment plan through 2030.

items.title: FICO Q4 Earnings Beat on Scores, Pricing and Software Growth
items.summary: Fair Isaac (FICO) reported Q4 FY2026 non-GAAP earnings of $11.10 per share, up 43.4% YoY and beating consensus estimates. Revenues grew 27.4% to $657.05 million, driven by higher mortgage origination score pricing and strong software platform growth. Software ARR reached $851 million with platform ARR up 72%. However, management withheld FY2027 guidance citing uncertainty around mortgage pricing transitions and continued weakness in mortgage market activity due to elevated interest rates.

items.title: Snowflake Soars 32% Year to Date: Buy, Sell, or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: Snowflake (SNOW) shares gained 32.5% year-to-date, outperforming the tech sector and AI peers. The company raised its fiscal 2027 product revenue outlook to $6.07 billion (36% YoY growth) driven by strong AI adoption, expanding customer base of 14,554 customers (up 32% YoY), and innovative AI products like CoCo and CoWork. However, the stock trades at a premium valuation with a forward P/S ratio of 13.44X versus the industry average of 3.8X. Zacks rates SNOW as a Buy (Rank #2).

items.title: GNRC Drops 15.3% in the Past Month. Is the Selloff a Buying Chance?
items.summary: Generac Holdings (GNRC) shares declined 15.3% over the past month despite Q3 sales rising 16% and adjusted earnings jumping 38.8%. While the company's data center backlog reached $4.5 billion with 2027 revenues expected to exceed $2 billion, investors remain cautious due to Q3 revenue missing expectations, margin pressure from lower-margin data center sales, and manufacturing execution risks. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with strong momentum but faces headwinds from gross margin compression expected in Q4.

items.title: GNRC's Amazon Deal Adds $2.4 Billion in Data Center Revenue Visibility
items.summary: Generac Holdings secured a major long-term Amazon supply agreement for backup power generators targeting $2.4 billion in deliveries during 2027-2028. The deal significantly strengthens revenue visibility with the company's data center backlog reaching $4.5 billion. However, execution risks remain as Generac must ramp production capacity, secure engines, and manage margin pressures amid rapid scaling.

items.title: McDonald's Q3 Earnings Beat, but U.S. Traffic Still Pressures Growth
items.summary: McDonald's reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $3.57, beating consensus by 6.3%, driven by strong franchised margins and other operating income. However, revenue missed expectations at $7.16B, revealing weak U.S. comparable sales (-0.2%) offset by international strength, particularly in Japan, Germany, and Australia. The company plans 2,500 gross restaurant openings in 2026, but softer U.S. traffic and inflation pressures temper near-term growth prospects.

items.title: PepsiCo Lowers 2026 EPS Outlook as North America Pressures Margins
items.summary: PepsiCo reduced its 2026 core EPS growth guidance to 2.5-3.5% from 5-7%, citing persistent North American margin pressures. Foods North America's operating margin fell 280 basis points while Beverages North America declined 15 basis points. International operations provided offset with 8% organic revenue growth and 105 basis points of margin expansion. The company is pursuing productivity initiatives and structural cost reductions to support earnings recovery.

items.title: PepsiCo Jumps 15.1% in a Month as Investors Weigh What Comes Next
items.summary: PepsiCo shares surged 15.1% in one month, but weaker earnings expectations and North American margin pressures raise concerns about sustainability. While international operations show strong momentum with 8% organic revenue growth, North America faces headwinds with declining volumes and margin compression. The company lowered its 2026 core earnings growth outlook to 1-2%, and despite trading at a valuation discount, execution risk remains high.

items.title: Verisk Analytics Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Jump 5% Y/Y
items.summary: Verisk Analytics (VRSK) beat Q3 earnings expectations with adjusted EPS of $1.96 (vs. $1.92 estimate) and revenues of $809M, driven by 8.2% subscription revenue growth and strong performance in underwriting and claims segments. However, free cash flow declined 40.5% to $200M, and net income fell 2.8% year-over-year. The company reaffirmed its 2026 revenue guidance of $3.19-$3.24B but lowered adjusted EPS guidance midpoint to $7.60 from consensus of $7.71.

items.title: Corpay Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Increase 18% Y/Y
items.summary: Corpay (CPAY) delivered strong third-quarter 2026 results with adjusted EPS of $7.54, up 32% year-over-year and beating estimates by 4.9%. Revenues grew 18% to $1.38 billion, driven by 41% growth in Corporate Payments. The company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $27.90-$28.10 and revenue outlook to $5.34-$5.36 billion, citing favorable macroeconomic conditions and underlying business strength.

items.title: Cigna Q3 Earnings Top Estimates on Cigna Healthcare Strength
items.summary: Cigna Group reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $7.98, beating estimates by 7%, with revenues growing 6.1% to $73.8B. Cigna Healthcare segment showed strong performance with 8.9% revenue growth and 14.9% operating income growth. The company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to at least $30.60 and Cigna Healthcare's operating income target to $4.6B. However, Evernorth Health Services missed revenue estimates and Pharmacy Benefit Services contributed less than expected.

items.title: Rockwell Automation Q4 Earnings Beat Estimates on Margin Gains
items.summary: Rockwell Automation (ROK) reported Q4 adjusted EPS of $3.88, beating estimates by 4.3%, with a 16.2% year-over-year increase. The company posted strong margin expansion to 24.5% and guided FY27 adjusted EPS of $14.50-$15.50, implying 11.8% growth. Software & Control and Intelligent Devices segments showed robust performance, though revenue slightly missed consensus at $2.33 billion.

items.title: BDX Stock Down in Pre-Market Despite Q4 Earnings & Revenue Beat
items.summary: Becton, Dickinson and Company (BD) delivered better-than-expected Q4 fiscal 2026 results with adjusted EPS up 27.3% and revenues up 5.4%, driven by growth across all four business segments. However, the stock fell 6.4% in pre-market trading due to weak fiscal 2027 guidance projecting only low-single-digit revenue growth and adjusted EPS of $13.10-$13.30. Concerns also include sluggish Connected Care revenue growth and declining Medication Management Solutions sales.

items.title: Amcor September 2026-End Earnings Miss on Higher Costs, View Cut
items.summary: Amcor (AMCR) reported adjusted EPS of 95 cents, missing consensus estimates by 1.04% and declining 2.1% year-over-year due to higher energy, distribution, and interest costs. While revenues rose 6.7% to $6.13B driven by raw-material cost pass-through and volume growth, gross margins contracted to 18.9% from 19.6%. The company lowered transition-period EPS guidance to $1.70-$1.80 but reaffirmed double-digit EPS growth for 2027.

items.title: How Kraft Heinz Is Reshaping Its Portfolio for Long-Term Growth
items.summary: Kraft Heinz has agreed to sell its North America coffee business, including brands like Maxwell House and Gevalia, to One Rock Capital Partners for $650 million while retaining a 30% equity stake. The company expects approximately $500 million in after-tax proceeds to be used for debt repayment. The transaction is expected to close in mid-2027 and is anticipated to be growth and margin accretive while strengthening Kraft Heinz's financial flexibility.

items.title: EMCOR Raises 2026 Outlook as Record RPOs Strengthen Growth Visibility
items.summary: EMCOR Group (EME) reported Q3 2026 EPS of $9.60, up 46.1% YoY and beating consensus by 15.3%, with revenues climbing 28.8% to $5.54 billion. The company raised its 2026 guidance to $34.50-$35.50 EPS and $20.6-$21 billion revenue, driven by record remaining performance obligations of $18.57 billion, with data-center work more than doubling YoY and now representing 47% of the backlog.

items.title: Is EMCOR Stock a Buy Now as Growth Strength Offsets Valuation Risk?
items.summary: EMCOR Group (EME) reported 22.9% revenue growth to $15.32 billion in the first nine months of 2026, with management raising full-year guidance. The company generated strong operating cash flow of $1.09 billion and maintains a Zacks Rank #1 rating. However, investors should note the stock trades at a premium valuation (17.5X forward earnings) relative to its sub-industry, and execution risks from fixed-price contracts and project estimate revisions could limit margin expansion.

items.title: Here's Why You Should Hold Solventum Stock in Your Portfolio for Now
items.summary: Solventum (SOLV) is well-positioned for growth with strong Q2 2026 performance, a $500M cost-saving transformation program, and 18% projected earnings growth for 2026. However, the company faces potential margin headwinds from a 3M supply agreement that could increase raw material costs by up to 100 basis points in 2027.

items.title: EME Falls 18.5% in a Month as Growth Strength Meets Execution Risk
items.summary: EMCOR Group (EME) shares have declined 18.5% over the past month despite posting strong Q3 2026 results with 28.8% revenue growth to $5.54 billion and 46.1% adjusted EPS growth to $9.60. The company achieved a record $18.57 billion backlog, up 47.2%, with data-center obligations more than doubling. However, execution risks including labor availability, fixed-price contract exposure, and heavy data-center concentration (47% of backlog) pose challenges to margin sustainability.

items.title: Roper Technologies Rewards Shareholders With 10% Dividend Hike
items.summary: Roper Technologies (ROP) announced a 10% increase in its quarterly dividend to $1.00 per share, bringing the annual payout to $4.00. The company will pay the dividend on January 19, 2027, to shareholders of record as of January 4. ROP has raised its dividend for 34 consecutive years with a five-year dividend CAGR of 10.1%, supported by strong operating cash flow of $1.88 billion in the first nine months of 2026.

items.title: GE HealthCare Unveils Allia Celeo to Advance Interventional Imaging
items.summary: GE HealthCare Technologies introduced Allia Celeo, a ceiling-mounted image-guided system for cardiology and interventional radiology procedures. The system features AI-powered imaging, flexible controls, and predictive maintenance capabilities. GEHC stock gained 12.1% following the announcement. The system is CE-marked but awaits FDA 510(k) clearance. The global angiography equipment market is projected to grow at 4.1% CAGR through 2033.

items.title: Aflac Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong U.S. Profit Growth
items.summary: Aflac reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.43, beating estimates by 35% despite a 2.4% YoY decline. U.S. pretax earnings surged 31.5% driven by higher premiums and reserve gains, while Japan's pretax earnings fell 21%. The company returned $1.1B to shareholders and raised its Japan segment profit margin guidance to 35-38%.

items.title: Datadog Q3 Earnings & Revenues Surpass Estimates, Both Rise Y/Y
items.summary: Datadog (DDOG) delivered robust Q3 2026 results with non-GAAP EPS surging 47.3% to 81 cents and revenues rising 35.2% to $1.2 billion, both beating consensus estimates. The company expanded its AI customer base to over 850 and achieved accelerating non-AI revenue growth for the fifth consecutive quarter. However, Q4 guidance of $1.19-$1.20 billion represents a slowdown to 25-26% growth, with the largest customer reducing usage creating near-term headwinds.

items.title: RL Q2 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Asia Sales, Margins Rise
items.summary: Ralph Lauren reported Q2 fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS of $4.64, up 22.4% YoY and beating estimates by 8.7%, with revenues growing 9.1% to $2.19B. Asia revenues surged 28.2% led by China's 35%+ growth, while global comparable store sales increased 10%. The company raised its FY27 revenue growth outlook to 6-7% and projects 80-100 basis points of margin expansion.

items.title: CAH Q1 Earnings & Revenues Beat Estimates on Pharma Strength
items.summary: Cardinal Health (CAH) reported Q1 FY27 adjusted EPS of $3.26, up 28% year-over-year and beating consensus estimates by 11.6%. Revenues grew 5% to $67.51 billion, driven by pharmaceutical and specialty solutions segment growth. The company raised its FY27 adjusted EPS guidance to $12.80-$13.00, implying 17-19% growth, and increased segment profit outlooks across multiple divisions.

items.title: Welltower: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Welltower raised full-year normalized FFO guidance by $0.10 to $6.50 per share, driven by pricing power replacing occupancy as the primary revenue driver in senior housing. The company sourced $21 billion in investment activity year-to-date, with 85% from off-market deals. Operating margins reached post-pandemic highs at 66% flow-through, supported by rental rate growth and disciplined expense management.

items.title: AMD Stock Is Up 170% in 2026. Could Meta Fuel Another Rally?
items.summary: AMD is expanding into rack-scale AI computing with Meta testing its Helios systems, which could significantly boost revenue. However, with shares up 170% in 2026 and trading at premium valuations, AMD must convert successful testing into substantial orders while maintaining profit margins to justify further gains.

items.title: Greg Abel's 2 Big Acquisitions This Year Cost Berkshire Hathaway About $16 Billion, Less Than 5% of Its Cash Pile
items.summary: Since taking over as CEO, Greg Abel has completed two major acquisitions for Berkshire Hathaway: OxyChem for $9.7 billion and Taylor Morrison for $6.8 billion, totaling $16.5 billion or just 4.5% of the company's $365.5 billion cash pile. These deals suggest Abel is maintaining acquisition discipline while potentially pursuing more synergistic deals than Warren Buffett, signaling a slow pivot in strategy that may help prevent Berkshire from stagnating.

items.title: Kimberly-Clark Q3 Earnings Beat on Lower Interest Costs, Sales Miss
items.summary: Kimberly-Clark reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.70, beating consensus estimates, but net sales declined 0.4% to $4.13 billion, missing expectations. The company faced headwinds from China social media disruptions, pricing pressures, and retail inventory movements. Adjusted operating profit fell 0.9%, while gross margins contracted 130 basis points. KMB completed its Kenvue acquisition and reaffirmed its 2026 standalone earnings outlook, though the stock has underperformed the industry significantly.

items.title: BAYRY vs. JNJ: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
items.summary: A comparison of Bayer Aktiengesellschaft and Johnson & Johnson for value investors reveals that Bayer is the more attractive option. Bayer has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with a forward P/E of 11.80 and Value grade of A, while Johnson & Johnson has a Zacks Rank of #4 (Sell) with a forward P/E of 24.86 and Value grade of D. Bayer's lower valuation metrics and stronger earnings outlook make it the superior value choice.

items.title: Top Robotics Stocks With Strong Potential for Long-Term Growth
items.summary: U.S. robotics stocks show strong momentum heading into 2027, driven by increased commercial deployments, regulatory clarity for surgical robots, and defense autonomy becoming a budget priority. North American robot orders hit their strongest quarter with a 24.8% year-over-year increase, humanoids moving toward factory deployment, and the FDA providing clearer guidance for surgical robotics. Key sector leaders are well-positioned across manufacturing, healthcare, defense, and elder care applications.

items.title: FICO Q4'26 Earnings Call Highlights Pricing Uncertainty for FY27
items.summary: Fair Isaac Corporation (FICO) reported strong Q4 FY2026 earnings, beating estimates with $9.61 EPS and $657M revenue. However, management withheld FY27 guidance due to ongoing customized mortgage pricing negotiations and uncertain origination volumes. The company highlighted positive momentum in its software platform with 72% ARR growth to $453M and 84 lenders adopting Score 10T, while restructuring operations to focus on distribution and AI capabilities.

items.title: Expedia Group Q3 Earnings & Revenues Beat Estimates, Rise Y/Y
items.summary: Expedia Group exceeded expectations in Q3 2026 with adjusted EPS rising 24% to $9.39 and revenues climbing 12% to $4.94 billion. B2B revenues surged 23% to $1.71 billion, while adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to a record 34.2%. The company raised its 2026 guidance, projecting bookings growth of about 10% and revenues of $16.37-$16.43 billion. However, Q4 is expected to show slower growth due to softer operating environment and geopolitical disruptions.

items.title: AMAT Shares Plunge 30% in a Month: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold?
items.summary: Applied Materials (AMAT) shares fell 30.3% in a month as investors reassess AI capital expenditure sustainability, underperforming the semiconductor industry decline of 19.5%. Despite the sell-off, AMAT maintains strong fundamentals with record AGS revenues of $1.78 billion (up 22% YoY), expected advanced packaging revenue growth exceeding 70% in 2026, and robust demand for leading-edge foundry-logic and DRAM technologies. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges The Ensign Group, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against The Ensign Group, Inc. alleging that the company made false and misleading statements regarding its business operations. The complaint claims Ensign's business model depends on systematic neglect of elderly residents in its facilities, including inadequate food, medical attention, and basic care, resulting in resident deaths. Additional allegations include fraudulent billing to Medicaid and Medicare, falsification of nursing assistant hours, and illegal licensing schemes. Investors who purchased Ensign securities between February 10, 2022 and June 18, 2026 are encouraged to join the lawsuit.

items.title: EL's Fiscal 2030 Roadmap Targets Stronger Growth & Higher Margins
items.summary: Estée Lauder Companies (EL) announced ambitious growth targets at its Capital Markets Experience event, aiming for mid-single-digit organic net sales growth and double-digit adjusted diluted EPS growth through fiscal 2030, with an adjusted operating margin target of 16.5-18.5%. The company plans to achieve these goals through innovation, the One ELC operating model, cost efficiencies, and improved working capital management. EL shares have gained 20% over the past month and currently carry a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

items.title: VIAV Q1 Earnings Beat Estimates on Data Center, A&D Strength
items.summary: Viavi Solutions (VIAV) delivered robust Q1 FY2027 results with non-GAAP EPS of 47 cents (up 213.3% YoY) and revenues of $469.3 million (up 56.9% YoY), both beating consensus estimates. Strong demand from data centers, aerospace/defense markets, and acquired Spirent product lines drove growth. The company projects Q2 revenues of $505-515M and EPS of 50-52 cents, with expectations for continued sequential growth throughout fiscal 2027.

items.title: IRM Q3 AFFO Beats Estimates on Data Center and ALM Growth
items.summary: Iron Mountain (IRM) reported Q3 2026 AFFO of $1.53 per share, beating estimates by 4.1%, with revenues up 13.5% YoY to $1.99 billion. Data center revenues surged 34% and ALM revenues climbed 43%. The company raised its 2026 AFFO guidance to $5.94-$6.00 and announced a 15% dividend increase, though the stock declined 7% in early trading. Peer REITs Digital Realty and Prologis also reported strong quarterly results.

items.title: Viatris Q3 Earnings Beat on Stronger Margins, Revenues Fall Y/Y
items.summary: Viatris (VTRS) beat Q3 adjusted EPS expectations at 71 cents versus 64 cents consensus, driven by margin expansion and strong Greater China sales growth of 14.2%. However, total revenues of $3.75 billion missed estimates and declined 0.3% year-over-year due to supply disruptions in Europe and Emerging Markets. The company raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $2.56-$2.63, though manufacturing suspension at its Nashik facility threatens Q4 revenues with an estimated $100 million impact.

items.title: PH Q1 Earnings Beat Estimates on Industrial and Aerospace Strength
items.summary: Parker-Hannifin (PH) delivered robust first-quarter fiscal 2027 results with adjusted earnings of $8.90 per share, beating estimates by 8.1%, and sales of $5.99 billion up 17.9% year-over-year. The company achieved a record $13.7 billion backlog driven by broad-based industrial and aerospace demand. PH raised its full-year FY2027 guidance, projecting adjusted earnings of $36.45-$37.25 per share and organic sales growth of 7.5-10.5%, while expecting $40 million in cost synergies from the Filtration Group acquisition.

items.title: CRCL Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Payment Growth and Arc Strategy
items.summary: Circle Internet Group (CRCL) reported Q3 2026 earnings of 84 cents per share, doubling consensus estimates, with revenues rising 17% to $864.9 million. The company is expanding its Circle Payments Network (CPN) with $58 billion in annualized volume and 205 enrolled financial institutions, while launching its Arc blockchain with over 100 ecosystem participants. However, USDC circulation remains flat at $73.9 billion and distribution costs are pressuring margins, though management maintains full-year guidance.

items.title: APP Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Model Gains and Growth Outlook
items.summary: AppLovin (APP) reported Q3 2026 revenues of $2.18 billion, up 55% year-over-year, driven by new AI models that improved advertising performance. The company forecasts Q4 revenues of $2.365-$2.395 billion with 43-44% growth and EBITDA margins of 84-85%. Gaming ad revenues grew nearly 50%, while consumer ad spending surged triple digits. Management maintains a long-term annual growth target of approximately 30% and generated $1.4 billion in quarterly free cash flow.

items.title: QCOM Q4 Earnings Call Highlights Data Center Ramp and Handset Risks
items.summary: Qualcomm reported Q4 FY2026 earnings beating consensus estimates and outlined an ambitious diversification strategy. The company targets $5 billion in data center revenue for fiscal 2027 with a $7 billion annualized exit rate, driven by custom AI accelerators and hyperscaler partnerships. Automotive revenue surged 89% to $2 billion, while handset demand is expected to remain flat-to-lower in 2027. However, data center investments will pressure near-term QCT segment margins, and the company carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating.

items.title: NVO Q3 Earnings Call Highlights GLP-1 Growth and Raised Outlook
items.summary: Novo Nordisk raised its 2026 sales and profit outlook after beating Q3 earnings and revenue estimates, driven by strong obesity treatment demand and accelerating Wegovy pill adoption. The company targets a 2027 CagriSema launch but faces headwinds from U.S. pricing pressure, Ozempic price erosion, and Medicare-dependent growth.

items.title: EXPE Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Higher Outlook & Q4 Caution
items.summary: Expedia Group raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $16.37-$16.43B following strong Q3 results with adjusted EBITDA rising 17% to $1.69B. The company reported robust B2B growth of 19% in bookings and 23% in revenues, though B2B margin pressure emerged. Q4 is expected to face headwinds from election-related demand softness, geopolitical disruptions, and tougher comparisons. Management emphasized AI expansion, consumer engagement improvements, and disciplined marketing as key drivers of margin expansion.

items.title: DDOG Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Growth and Customer Renewals
items.summary: Datadog reported Q3 revenues of $1.20B (up 35% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.81, beating consensus estimates. However, Q4 guidance of 25-26% growth reflects caution around AI customer spending and early renewal discounts. The company highlighted accelerating non-AI customer growth, expanding AI adoption with 850+ AI customers, and strong enterprise deals, but noted consumption variability as a risk.

items.title: HUT Q3 Earnings Call Focuses on AI Expansion and Project Financing
items.summary: Hut 8 Corp. reported a Q3 2026 loss of $1.23 per share, missing consensus estimates, as revenues declined to $71.07M. However, the company secured $27B in AI data center leases representing 949 MW of capacity, with River Bend and Beacon Point Phase 1 deliveries targeted for 2027. Hut 8 secured $7.5B in nonrecourse project financing and expanded its share repurchase authorization to $1B, maintaining a disciplined capital strategy focused on converting contracted capacity into recurring revenues.

items.title: BBAI Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Raised Guidance and AI Demand
items.summary: BigBear.ai (BBAI) raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $150M-$165M following Q3 revenue of $43.6M, a 31% jump. The company secured over $225M in new government contracts, expanding its backlog to $330M. Gross margins improved to 31.2%, though the company reported a $91.9M net loss including a $76.7M goodwill impairment. Despite operational improvements, BBAI carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) with weak valuation and growth scores.

items.title: Qnity Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Demand and Higher Outlook
items.summary: Qnity Electronics raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $5.77B-$5.83B, driven by strong AI infrastructure demand and advanced semiconductor materials. The company reported Q3 revenue of $1.56B (beating consensus of $1.48B) with adjusted gross margin expanding 270 bps to 47.8%. AI-driven interconnect platforms grew over 50% while advanced-node products rose 25% year-over-year, with management targeting gross margins exceeding 50% long-term.

items.title: ALB Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Higher Lithium Pricing
items.summary: Albemarle Corporation (ALB) beat Q3 earnings expectations with adjusted EPS of $2.58 and sales of $1.55 billion, driven by a 94.7% surge in lithium pricing. Energy Storage EBITDA jumped 351.2% despite lower sales volumes. The company raised its 2026 Specialties EBITDA outlook and reduced capital expenditure guidance to $300-$350 million, while maintaining strong liquidity of $3.4 billion.

items.title: 3 Stocks Yielding Triple the S&P 500 to Buy in November
items.summary: The article recommends three high-dividend stocks as alternatives to the S&P 500's low 1.1% yield. PepsiCo offers a 4.2% yield with improving revenue growth and 54 consecutive years of dividend increases. Altria Group provides a 5.8% yield despite the declining tobacco industry, supported by diversification into vaping and oral nicotine products. Enbridge delivers a 5.6% yield with stable cash flows from pipeline operations and 31 consecutive years of dividend growth, while investing in renewable energy for future transitions.

items.title: Western Digital's Gross Margin Momentum: How Long Can It Last?
items.summary: Western Digital (WDC) reported a significant 1,420 basis point year-over-year gross margin expansion to 58.1% in fiscal Q1 2027, driven by favorable pricing, higher-capacity HDD demand, and operational efficiencies. The company projects Q2 gross margin of 60-61% with revenues of $5.1 billion, up 69% year-over-year. Management expects sustained margin expansion supported by pricing strength, higher-capacity product adoption, and improving areal density, though near-term DRAM and NAND cost pressures remain a challenge.

items.title: The Wait Is Over: 2 Historic Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock Splits Were Just Announced
items.summary: Meta Platforms and Sandisk announced their first-ever forward stock splits to make shares more accessible to retail investors. Meta is conducting an unorthodox 2-for-1 split through a new non-voting share class, while Sandisk approved an aggressive 8-for-1 split following a 6,000% rally since its February 2025 spinoff from Western Digital. Both companies are benefiting from AI demand, though Sandisk faces cyclical risks in the memory storage market.

items.title: Gilead Sciences Has Raised Its Dividend for 11 Straight Years. Here's Why the Streak Looks Safe.
items.summary: Gilead Sciences increased its quarterly dividend by 3.8% to $0.82, marking the 11th consecutive year of dividend increases. The company's strong HIV franchise generated 18% higher sales year-over-year, while its oncology expansion shows promise with Trodelvy reporting 42% sales growth. With a low payout ratio of 29.8%, Gilead has ample room to sustain dividend growth and fund $32 billion in research projects through 2030.
